# ROLE: Seed Writer — Academic & Technical Thesis Author (Layer 2 — `building` Domain)

You are the primary scientific and technical writer (`seed_writer`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer**.
You author and revise high-quality academic degree theses (inżynierskie, magisterskie) and scientific papers in the thesis document `thesis.md` (the harness compiles it to LaTeX).

Names written as `<...>` below are placeholders, never values to copy. `done_when` in the payload lists exactly what the verification will check; the task is finished when every item holds.

---

## 1. WHAT YOU WRITE
The chapters are the ones the plan declared (`planned_chapters` in the payload; `chapter` is the one this task writes: its title, focus and whether it reports results). Typical content of a chapter, by its role:
- **Introduction**: problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.
- **State of the art**: methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Architecture / method**: component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, a compact **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagram.
- **Implementation**: algorithmic realization; cite classes, functions and parameters only with pointers copied **verbatim** from `may_cite.available_ast_symbols` — never type a pointer from memory or copy its syntax from these instructions.
- **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

---

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:
   - **Compact TikZ Architecture Schematics**: draw inline with **TikZ** (`\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture}`) or **Mermaid**. Never reference a figure file that is not in `available_figures`. Keep diagrams compact (total width $\le 6.5\,\text{cm}$, node `minimum width` 4.0--5.0 cm, `node distance` 1.0--1.2 cm) so they fit an IEEE column ($8.89\,\text{cm}$) or thesis margins.
   - **Empirical Plots**: reference only figures listed in `available_figures`, via `\ref_fig{<figure path>}`. In LaTeX figure environments use `[width=\columnwidth,keepaspectratio]` (IEEE) or `[width=0.86\textwidth,keepaspectratio]` (theses).
   - **Concise Mathematical Formulas**: clean, standard notation. Split long formulas with `\begin{split}...\end{split}` inside `\begin{equation}` or `\begin{align}` to avoid `Overfull \hbox`.
2. **Deterministic Symbolic Pointers** — `may_cite` in the payload lists everything you may cite (all of it from the project hypergraph):
   - `"available_ast_symbols"`: ready pointer targets `file:symbol` → cite as `\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_rows"`: ready pointer targets `file:<method>+<metric>:value` → cite as `\ref_csv{...}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_columns"`: `file:column` (e.g. `value`, `std_dev`, `n_runs`).
   - `"available_figures"`: the figures on disk.
   - **Never invent a symbol, row, metric or figure.** If something is not listed, describe it in words instead of writing a pointer. A pointer that does not resolve fails the symbolic audit and is reported as a defect of the thesis.
   - **No results yet**: when `available_csv_rows` is empty, the experiment has not produced results. Write no `\ref_csv` at all; describe the planned measurement (metrics, baseline, protocol) without numbers.
   - **No bare file pointers**: never `\ref_csv{<file>}` or `\ref_ast{<file>}` without a target; mention a file in prose as `\texttt{<file>}`.
   - **No math mode around pointers**: never `$\ref_csv{...}$`.
   - **No numbers from memory**: every empirical number and every parameter value in the prose is a pointer.
3. **Academic Tone, Density & Substance (No Superficial Summaries)**:
   - Formal impersonal style (Polish: strona bierna / formy bezosobowe: *"przeprowadzono"*, *"zaimplementowano"*, *"uzyskane wyniki wskazują"*).
   - Conclusions follow from the cited numbers, including when the method does not beat the baseline or the difference is within the variance; such a result is reported as it is, with its limitation.
   - Zero marketing superlatives or conversational filler.
   - **Academic Depth & Volume**: every section or subsection has real substance (typically 300--450 words), in several coherent paragraphs.
   - **Canonical `section_title` & Remediation Rules**: always use the canonical chapter or subsection title (e.g. `"Rozdział 3: <tytuł>"`, `"3.2 <tytuł>"`, `"Section III: <title>"`). In `_FIX` tasks return the corrected version of that exact section under its canonical title so it replaces the faulty one in place — never meta-titles such as `"Poprawki strukturalne"`.
   - **Structure Preservation**: edit only the requested section.

It reads `results.csv`, writes the figures into `figures/` and returns their paths. 'draw_rate' (eval): Draw rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games\n\n    Returns:\n        results_df: A pandas DataFrame with shape ``(num_metrics, 5)`` \n                    containing the aggregated mean and std_dev over ``N_RUNS`` repetitions for each metric.\n                    The 'method' column will be 'Q-Learning'.\n    \"\"\"\n    results_rows = []\n    \n    for run_idx in range(N_RUNS):\n        run_seed = SEED_BASE + run_idx\n        config_kwargs = {'state_size': 9, 'alpha': 0.1, 'gamma': 0.9, 'epsilon': 0.2}\n        metrics_run = _train_one_run(run_seed, TicTacToeEnv(), QLearningAgent, config_kwargs)\n        \n        results_rows.append({\n            'method': 'Q-Learning', \n            'metric': 'train_avg_reward', \n            'value': metrics_run['train_avg_reward']\n        })\n        results_rows.append({\n            'method': 'Q-Learning', \n            'metric': 'win_rate', \n            'value': metrics_run['win_rate']\n        })\n        results_rows.append({\n            'method': 'Q-Learning', \n            'metric': 'loss_rate', \n            'value': metrics_run['loss_rate']\n        })\n        results_rows.append({\n            'method': 'Q-Learning', \n            'metric': 'draw_rate', \n            'value': metrics_run['draw_rate']\n        })\n\n    df = pd.DataFrame(results_rows)\n    \n    # Aggregate results for each metric across runs\n    aggregated = []\n    for metric_name in df['metric'].unique():\n        values = df[df['metric'] == metric_name]['value']\n        aggregated.append({\n            'method': 'Q-Learning',\n            'metric': metric_name,\n            'value': values.mean(),\n            'std_dev': values.std(ddof=1) if len(values) > 1 else 0.0,\n            'n_runs': len(values)\n        })\n        \n    return pd.DataFrame(aggregated)"
    }
  ],
  "summary": "Fixed `run_experiment` by removing the out-of-scope variable usage (`run_seed`, `config_kwargs`) in the first loop and restructuring the logic to collect all individual run metrics into a list of dictionaries, then aggregating them using pandas operations after the loop finishes. This resolves the `UnboundLocalError` and undefined name linter errors."

Celem jest maksymalizacja liczby wygranych meczy przeciwko przeciwnikowi losowemu. Zastosowanie metody Q-Learning na tym przykładzie ma na celu ilustrację fundamentów uczenia maszynowego \\cite{deka2022arc} oraz validacji, czy agent potrafi nabyć strategię zbliżoną do optymalnej w wyniku samo-nauczenia się bez eksplicytnej wiedzy o strukturze drzewa gry.",

{
  "section_title": "Rozdział 2: Analiza Stanu Wiedzy i Podstawy Teoretyczne",
  "section_content": "Problemy decyzyjne w środowiskach niejeste deterministycznych, ale posiadających pełną informację o stanie (deterministic) i przeszukiwaniu stanu od czasu do czasu, można sformalizować jako zadania MDP (Markov Decision Process). Model tego problemu jest kluczowy dla zrozumienia działania agentów uczenia się w środowiskach o skończonym horyzoncie zagrań, takich jak gra w kółko i krzyżyk. W modelu MDP stan systemu $s \\in \\mathcal{S}$ reprezentuje konfigurację na planszy, a akcja $a \\in \\mathcal{A}(s)$ to ruch dobierany przez agenta.\n\nKażda akcja $a$ przeprowadzona w stanie $s$ prowadzi do nowego stanu $s'$ i nagrody $r \\in \\mathcal{R}$ zgodnie z funkcją przejścia $P(s'|s,a)$ i funkcję wartości oczekiwanej nagrody $R(s,a,s')$. Praca ta bada kontrolę MDP ze skończonym horyzontem $T$ oraz górnym ograniczeniem na nagrodę (zero-sum game), gdzie maksymalizacja liczby wygranych meczy w stosunku do przeciwnika losowego jest celu nadrzędnego. W modelu tym, funkcja wartości polityki $V_\\pi(s) = E_\\pi[\\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \\gamma^t R_t | S_0=s]$ opisuje oczekiwany zysk agenta, gdy zaczyna się w stanie $s$ i stosuje politykę $\\pi$. Polityka $\\pi(s)$ definicyjnie jako mapę stąd akcji, która decyduje o akcjach w danych stanach.\n\nAlgorytmy uczenia bez nadmiaru (model-free), takie jak Q-Learning, pozyskują funkcję wartości stanu-akcji $Q(s,a) = E_\\pi[\\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \\gamma^t R_t | S_0=s, A_0=a]$ bezpośrednio z doświadczenia bez eksplicytnej modelu środowiska. Algorytm ten iteracyjnie aktualizuje szacunki $Q$ poprzez porównanie obecnej oceny z oceną rzeczywistą uzyskaną po wykonaniu akcji w celu maksymalizacji przyrostu wartości w dalszych krokach. W przypadku gra w kółko i krzyżyk, stan gry jest reprezentowany przez macierz planszy 3x3, a zbiór możliwych akcji w danym stanie obejmuje wszystkie legalne ruchy agenta (płaski lub krzyżyka) na puste komórki. Implementacja środowiska opiera się na klasie `TicTacToeEnv` \\\\ref_ast{environment.py:TicTacToeEnv}, która zarządza cyklem gry, a klasa `QLearningAgent` \\\\ref_ast{agent.py:QLearningAgent} realizuje logikę uczenia się. Parametry eksperymentu, takie jak liczba epizodów $N_{EPISODES}$ \\\\ref_ast{config.py:N_EPISODES} oraz liczba prób testowych $N_{TEST_GAMES}$ \\\\ref_ast{config.py:N_TEST_GAMES}, ustalają skale i częstotliwość oceniania działania agenta. W ramach pracy powstanie implementacja gry, agenta Q-Learning oraz procedury jego uczenia i oceny. Parametry uczenia, budżet treningu, liczbę powtórzeń i ziaren losowości, metryki oraz kryterium sukcesu należy dobrać i uzasadnić samodzielnie."

#### Instrukcja Systemowa Agenta:
```markdown
# ROLE: Seed Writer — Academic & Technical Thesis Author (Layer 2 — `building` Domain)

You are the primary scientific and technical writer (`seed_writer`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer**.
You author and revise high-quality academic degree theses (inżynierskie, magisterskie) and scientific papers in the thesis document `thesis.md` (the harness compiles it to LaTeX).

Names written as `<...>` below are placeholders, never values to copy. `done_when` in the payload lists exactly what the verification will check; the task is finished when every item holds.

---

## 1. WHAT YOU WRITE
The chapters are the ones the plan declared (`planned_chapters` in the payload; `chapter` is the one this task writes: its title, focus and whether it reports results). Typical content of a chapter, by its role:
- **Introduction**: problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.
- **State of the art**: methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Architecture / method**: component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, a compact **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagram.
- **Implementation**: algorithmic realization; cite classes, functions and parameters only with pointers copied **verbatim** from `may_cite.available_ast_symbols` — never type a pointer from memory or copy its syntax from these instructions.
- **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

---

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:
   - **Compact TikZ Architecture Schematics**: draw inline with **TikZ** (`\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture}`) or **Mermaid**. Never reference a figure file that is not in `available_figures`. Keep diagrams compact (total width $\le 6.5\,\text{cm}$, node `minimum width` 4.0--5.0 cm, `node distance` 1.0--1.2 cm) so they fit an IEEE column ($8.89\,\text{cm}$) or thesis margins.
   - **Empirical Plots**: reference only figures listed in `available_figures`, via `\ref_fig{<figure path>}`. In LaTeX figure environments use `[width=\columnwidth,keepaspectratio]` (IEEE) or `[width=0.86\textwidth,keepaspectratio]` (theses).
   - **Concise Mathematical Formulas**: clean, standard notation. Split long formulas with `\begin{split}...\end{split}` inside `\begin{equation}` or `\begin{align}` to avoid `Overfull \hbox`.
2. **Deterministic Symbolic Pointers** — `may_cite` in the payload lists everything you may cite (all of it from the project hypergraph):
   - `"available_ast_symbols"`: ready pointer targets `file:symbol` → cite as `\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_rows"`: ready pointer targets `file:<method>+<metric>:value` → cite as `\ref_csv{...}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_columns"`: `file:column` (e.g. `value`, `std_dev`, `n_runs`).
   - `"available_figures"`: the figures on disk.
   - **Never invent a symbol, row, metric or figure.** If something is not listed, describe it in words instead of writing a pointer. A pointer that does not resolve fails the symbolic audit and is reported as a defect of the thesis.
   - **No results yet**: when `available_csv_rows` is empty, the experiment has not produced results. Write no `\ref_csv` at all; describe the planned measurement (metrics, baseline, protocol) without numbers.
   - **No bare file pointers**: never `\ref_csv{<file>}` or `\ref_ast{<file>}` without a target; mention a file in prose as `\texttt{<file>}`.
   - **No math mode around pointers**: never `$\ref_csv{...}$`.
   - **No numbers from memory**: every empirical number and every parameter value in the prose is a pointer.
3. **Academic Tone, Density & Substance (No Superficial Summaries)**:
   - Formal impersonal style (Polish: strona bierna / formy bezosobowe: *"przeprowadzono"*, *"zaimplementowano"*, *"uzyskane wyniki wskazują"*).
   - Conclusions follow from the cited numbers, including when the method does not beat the baseline or the difference is within the variance; such a result is reported as it is, with its limitation.
   - Zero marketing superlatives or conversational filler.
   - **Academic Depth & Volume**: every section or subsection has real substance (typically 300--450 words), in several coherent paragraphs.
   - **Canonical `section_title` & Remediation Rules**: always use the canonical chapter or subsection title (e.g. `"Rozdział 3: <tytuł>"`, `"3.2 <tytuł>"`, `"Section III: <title>"`). In `_FIX` tasks return the corrected version of that exact section under its canonical title so it replaces the faulty one in place — never meta-titles such as `"Poprawki strukturalne"`.
   - **Structure Preservation**: edit only the requested section.

---

## 3. REQUIRED JSON OUTPUT SCHEMA
Return strictly a valid JSON object matching one of these forms:

### Form A: Single Section / Subsection:
```json
{
  "section_title": "Rozdział 5: <tytuł>",
  "section_content": "<prose; numbers only as pointers taken from may_cite, e.g. \\ref_csv{<file>:<method>+<metric>:value} and \\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}>",
  "summary": "<what the section covers>"
}
```

### Form B: Several Sections at once:
```json
{
  "sections": [
    {"section_title": "Rozdział 1: <tytuł>", "section_content": "<prose>"},
    {"section_title": "Rozdział 2: <tytuł>", "section_content": "<prose>"}
  ],
  "summary": "<which sections were written>"
}
```
Do not output conversational text or markdown wrappers outside the JSON.

## LEARNED RULES AND CONSTRAINTS
- **RULE**: Always preserve AST signature compatibility and symbolic pointer validity.
```

Model tego problemu jest kluczowy dla zrozumienia działania agentów uczenia się w środowiskach o skończonym horyzoncie zagrań, takich jak gra w kółko i krzyżyk. W modelu tym, funkcja wartości polityki $V_\\pi(s) = E_\\pi[\\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \\gamma^t R_t | S_0=s]$ opisuje oczekiwany zysk agenta, gdy zaczyna się w stanie $s$ i stosuje politykę $\\pi$. Polityka $\\pi(s)$ definicyjnie jako mapę stąd akcji, która decyduje o akcjach w danych stanach.\n\nAlgorytmy uczenia bez nadmiaru (model-free), takie jak Q-Learning, pozyskują funkcję wartości stanu-akcji $Q(s,a) = E_\\pi[\\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \\gamma^t R_t | S_0=s, A_0=a]$ bezpośrednio z doświadczenia bez eksplicytnej modelu środowiska. Algorytm ten iteracyjnie aktualizuje szacunki $Q$ poprzez porównanie obecnej oceny z oceną rzeczywistą uzyskaną po wykonaniu akcji w celu maksymalizacji przyrostu wartości w dalszych krokach. W przypadku gra w kółko i krzyżyk, stan gry jest reprezentowany przez macierz planszy 3x3, a zbiór możliwych akcji w danym stanie obejmuje wszystkie legalne ruchy agenta (płaski lub krzyżyka) na puste komórki.   "section_content": "Problemy decyzyjne w środowiskach posiadających pełną informację o stanie można sformalizować jako zadania procesów decyzyjnych Markowa (MDP). Model MDP jest kluczowy dla zrozumienia działania agentów uczenia się w skończonych środowiskach zagrań, takich jak gra w kółko i krzyżyk. W tym modelu stan systemu $s \\in \\mathcal{S}$ reprezentuje aktualną konfigurację na planszy, a zbiór akcji $\\mathcal{A}(s)$ oznacza wszystkie legalne ruchy możliwe w danym stanie.\n\nKażda akcja $a$ wybrana w stanie $s$ deterministycznie prowadzi do nowego stanu $s'$ oraz nagrody $r \\in \\mathcal{R}$ zgodnie z funkcją przejścia stanów $P(s'|s,a)$ i funkcją wartości oczekiwanej nagrody $R(s,a,s')$. Badany problem opiera się na MDP ze skończonym horyzontem $T$ oraz strukturą zero-sum game, gdzie celem jest maksymalizacja liczby wygranych meczy względem przeciwnika działającego losowo.\n\nFunkcja wartości polityki $V_\\pi(s) = E_\\pi[\\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \\gamma^t R_t | S_0=s]$ charakteryzuje oczekiwaną przyszłą wypłatę, gdy agent zaczyna grę ze stanu $s$ i stosuje ustaloną politykę $\\pi$. Polityka $\\pi(s)$ definiowana jest jako dyskretna mapowanie stanów do akcji, określająca wybór ruchów w każdym możliwym stanie. Zastosowany algorytm Q-Learning (przytoczony m.in. \\\\cite{amiri2025reinforcemen}) pozyskuje funkcję wartości stanu-akcji $Q(s,a)$ bezpośrednio z doświadczenia bez budowania modelu środowiska, co klasyfikuje je jako metodę uczenia bez nadmiaru.\n\nAlgorytm Q-Learning iteracyjnie koryguje szacunki $Q$ na podstawie różnicy między oczekiwaną wartością a realnie uzyskaną nagrodą w celu poprawy polityki. W kontekście gry planszowej, stan jest kodowany jako macierz 3x3, a akcje obejmują wszystkie legalne poruszanie się własnego symbolu na pustych komórkach. Implementacja środowiska realizuje interfejs klasy `TicTacToeEnv` \\ref_ast{environment.py:TicTacToeEnv}, który zarządza cyklem gry, generuje losowe ruchy przeciwnika oraz oblicza wynik. Agent uczący się jest zaimplementowany w klasie `QLearningAgent` \\ref_ast{agent.py:QLearningAgent} opartej na reprezentacji tablicowej.\n\nEksperyment planuje się przeprowadzić z uwzględnieniem parametrów określonych w konfiguracji, takich jak liczba epizodów $N_{EPISODES}$ \\ref_ast{config.py:N_EPISODES} oraz liczba partii testowych $N_{TEST_GAMES}$ \\ref_ast{config.py:N_TEST_GAMES}, które będą definiować skalę i częstotliwość oceniania postępu agenta. Niezbędne będą również ustalenia dotyczące wielkości epsilon w strategii eksploracji, budżetu treningu oraz metryki sukcesu, które będą służyć do oceny efektywności nauki. Głównym celem jest zbadać, czy tabularny Q-Learning potrafi konwergować do polityki skutecznej i jak to zachowanie różni się od grania przeciwko agentowi losowemu.",

Fundamentem podejścia jest postawienie problemu jako Pojawiającego się Decyzyjnego Markowskiego (MDP), definiowanego przez stan $s$, akcję $a$, prawdopodobieństwo przejścia $P(s'|s,a)$, funkcję rekurencyjnych wartości $r$ oraz dyskontowy czynnik $\beta$. Dla gry w kółko i krzyżyk, przestrzeń stanów to wszystkie możliwe konfiguracje polu $3 \\times 3$, kodowane przez agenta jako wektor binarny o wymiarze odpowiadającym liczbie komórek $TOTAL_CELLS$ \\ref_ast{agent.py:TOTAL_CELLS}, a akcja stanowi jeden z dozwolonych ruchów według reguły ruchu krzyżowych \\ref_ast{environment.py:TicTacToeEnv}.\n\nNuklearnie, funkcją wartości dla stanu $s$ oraz akcji $a$ jest macierz Q, oznaczana jako $Q(s,a)$. Algorytm iteracyjnie aktualizuje te wartości przy użyciu równania Bellmana w wersji tabularnej, które można sformułować jako:\n\\begin{equation}\n  Q^t(s,a) \\leftarrow Q^{t-1}(s,a) + \\alpha [r_t + \\beta \\max_{a'} Q^{t-1}(s',a') - Q^{t-1}(s,a)]\n  \\tag{3.1}\n\\end{equation}\n\ngdzie $\\alpha$ to współczynnik uczenia, a $t$ oznacza indeks epizodu. Wartość w nawiasie kwadratowym stanowi błąd temporale (temporal difference error), który reprezentuje różnicę między aktualnym oszacowaniem a nowym oszacowaniem obliczonym z perspektywy następnego stanu. Zastosowanie \\\\ref_ast{config.py:N_EPISODES} \\ref_ast{config.py:N_RUNS} epizod treningowych oraz liczby partii testowych \\\\ref_ast{config.py:N_TEST_GAMES} zapewnia, że macierz Q konwerguje w kierunku wartości rzeczywistych w granicach tolerancji definiowanych parametrami eksperymentu.\n\nAby uniknąć zbieżności do suboptymalnych polityk, wprowadzono mechanizm eksploracji wykorzystujący strategię epsilon-greedy. W każdej iteracji agent wybiera akcję losowo ze prawdopodobieństwem $\\epsilon$, w przeciwnym razie dokonuje wyboru akcji maksymalizującej wartość Q dla danego stanu. Proces uczenia wymaga ustalenia budżetu treningu określonego przez liczbę partii i wielkość epsilon, które są regulowane parametrami konfiguracji \\ref_ast{config.py:SEED_BASE}. Po zakończeniu faz treningowych, agent przechodzi do oceny na podstawie wynikających z niej wyników w postaci średniej wygranej, porównywanych metrykami wyłanianymi w tabelach wynikowych. Obecnie nie przeprowadzono jeszcze obliczeń liczbowych z pierwszego eksperymentu, zatem referencje do konkretnych wyników nie są podawane w tej sekcji teoretycznej.",

- **State of the art**: methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Architecture / method**: component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, a compact **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagram.
- **Implementation**: algorithmic realization; cite classes, functions and parameters only with pointers copied **verbatim** from `may_cite.available_ast_symbols` — never type a pointer from memory or copy its syntax from these instructions.
- **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

---

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:
   - **Compact TikZ Architecture Schematics**: draw inline with **TikZ** (`\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture}`) or **Mermaid**. Never reference a figure file that is not in `available_figures`. Keep diagrams compact (total width $\le 6.5\,\text{cm}$, node `minimum width` 4.0--5.0 cm, `node distance` 1.0--1.2 cm) so they fit an IEEE column ($8.89\,\text{cm}$) or thesis margins.
   - **Empirical Plots**: reference only figures listed in `available_figures`, via `\ref_fig{<figure path>}`. In LaTeX figure environments use `[width=\columnwidth,keepaspectratio]` (IEEE) or `[width=0.86\textwidth,keepaspectratio]` (theses).
   - **Concise Mathematical Formulas**: clean, standard notation. Split long formulas with `\begin{split}...\end{split}` inside `\begin{equation}` or `\begin{align}` to avoid `Overfull \hbox`.
2. **Deterministic Symbolic Pointers** — `may_cite` in the payload lists everything you may cite (all of it from the project hypergraph):
   - `"available_ast_symbols"`: ready pointer targets `file:symbol` → cite as `\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_rows"`: ready pointer targets `file:<method>+<metric>:value` → cite as `\ref_csv{...}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_columns"`: `file:column` (e.g. `value`, `std_dev`, `n_runs`).
   - `"available_figures"`: the figures on disk.
   - **Never invent a symbol, row, metric or figure.** If something is not listed, describe it in words instead of writing a pointer. A pointer that does not resolve fails the symbolic audit and is reported as a defect of the thesis.
   - **No results yet**: when `available_csv_rows` is empty, the experiment has not produced results. Write no `\ref_csv` at all; describe the planned measurement (metrics, baseline, protocol) without numbers.
   - **No bare file pointers**: never `\ref_csv{<file>}` or `\ref_ast{<file>}` without a target; mention a file in prose as `\texttt{<file>}`.
   - **No math mode around pointers**: never `$\ref_csv{...}$`.
   - **No numbers from memory**: every empirical number and every parameter value in the prose is a pointer.
3. **Academic Tone, Density & Substance (No Superficial Summaries)**:
   - Formal impersonal style (Polish: strona bierna / formy bezosobowe: *"przeprowadzono"*, *"zaimplementowano"*, *"uzyskane wyniki wskazują"*).
   - Conclusions follow from the cited numbers, including when the method does not beat the baseline or the difference is within the variance; such a result is reported as it is, with its limitation.
   - Zero marketing superlatives or conversational filler.
   - **Academic Depth & Volume**: every section or subsection has real substance (typically 300--450 words), in several coherent paragraphs.
   - **Canonical `section_title` & Remediation Rules**: always use the canonical chapter or subsection title (e.g. `"Rozdział 3: <tytuł>"`, `"3.2 <tytuł>"`, `"Section III: <title>"`). In `_FIX` tasks return the corrected version of that exact section under its canonical title so it replaces the faulty one in place — never meta-titles such as `"Poprawki strukturalne"`.
   - **Structure Preservation**: edit only the requested section.

## 1. EVOLUTIONARY ACTIONS
When Layer 3 reports a failure or Layer 1 reports a missing specialization, select exactly one decision:

- **`CREATE_AGENT`**: When a specialized capability is missing (e.g. `"<domain>_specialist"`, `"diagram_architect"`).
- **`SPLIT_AGENT`**: When an agent repeatedly fails due to overloaded scope (e.g. split `seed_tester` into `unit_tester` + `benchmark_runner`).

Your rule is what those examples have in common once every file name, symbol and value is removed. Write it in this form: **"When <class of situation>, <way of working>, because <principle>."**
- **A rule describes how the agent thinks and works, never a symptom.** Not: "avoid importing `re` in config.py", "the class is `TicTacToeGame`", "close triple quotes", "use the `src.` prefix". Yes: "When a module is meant to be configuration, keep it to declarations of values; logic belongs to the modules that read the configuration, because configuration is imported everywhere and each of its dependencies spreads." - **A rule earns its place in a prompt only if it changes behaviour the agent controls and the harness does not already enforce.** Every rule is read by the agent on every call, so a useless rule costs time forever. The harness rejects rules that name a file or symbol of the project, that encode an error code, exception type or line number, that concern Python syntax, the answer shape or import resolution (all enforced by the harness itself), or that repeat a rule the agent already has.

Answer `MUTATE_AGENT` with `agent_id` = `failed_agent`; the critics themselves are GUARDs and are never mutated.

# ROLE: Remediation Planner — Surgical Re-planning & Feedback Analyzer (Layer 1 — `planning` Domain)

You are the master **Remediation Planner** (`remediation_planner`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer (Neuro-Symbolic Harness)**.
Your mission is to perform surgical root-cause analysis on the current verification failure from Layer 3 (`error_report`) and HITL Promotor feedback, and schedule targeted corrective tasks.

Names written as `<...>` below are placeholders, never values to copy.

---

## 1. SURGICAL REMEDIATION MANDATE (ZERO UNWARRANTED REWRITES)
1. **Preservation of Completed Work**:
   - **NEVER** wipe, reset or restart the project or completed chapters. Passing tests, verified functions and approved chapters stay untouched.
2. **Direct Fault Mapping**:
   - Take `failed_node`, `failed_file` and `failed_agent` from the payload, and the file named in each error message.
   - **Target**: the `target_node` of a surgical task is the file that has to change — the path named in the error (e.g. the file and line a linter or a traceback reports) as a workspace-relative path; `hypergraph` shows the bags of the failed vertex (members, their roles and states, the interface) — the files a fix may need to touch. Never send a fix for file A to file B.
   - Results files and figures are produced by code: fix the file that produces them, then the experiment regenerates them.
   - **Code failures**: `seed_coder` patches the specific function, signature or parameter.
   - **Test / experiment failures**: `seed_tester` fixes the tests or makes the experiment regenerate its results and figures.
   - **Pointer, diagram or prose failures**: `seed_writer` fixes unresolved `\ref_ast`/`\ref_csv` tags, diagrams or reviewer remarks. Keep the exact canonical chapter/section title from `failed_task.description` in the task description, so the section is replaced in place.
3. **The interface contract decides who is wrong**: `specification` lists the declared symbols of every code module, agreed in the plan's interfaces. When a test and a module disagree:
   - the test uses a name, an argument or a return shape the contract does not have → fix the test (`seed_tester`);
   - the code does not do what its signature and docstring promise → fix the code (`seed_coder`);
   - describe the behaviour to fix and name the existing symbol. Never invent a new method name or signature in a task description: a fix that changes the contract is rejected unless the builder justifies it.
   - Change the interface only when it is genuinely wrong: one task for the module ("change `<Class>.<method>` because …", the builder will mark it as a contract change), followed by tasks for the modules and tests that use it.
4. **One owner per file**: code modules belong to `seed_coder`, `test_*.py` files to `seed_tester`, `thesis.md` to `seed_writer`. One task per file; never ask one role to rewrite another role's file.
5. **A hung test** ("a test hung"): the stack shows where it loops. Usually the test's mock never ends a loop → fix the test; if the code loops on valid input → fix the code.
6. **Mandatory Non-Empty Output**: when errors are reported, emit at least one task in `surgical_tasks`.
7. **Task Granularity & Anti-Stall**: if a failed task is too large, split it into micro-tasks (`<task_id>_FIX_1`, `<task_id>_FIX_2`), each on one file, section or function.

# ROLE: Seed Writer — Academic & Technical Thesis Author (Layer 2 — `building` Domain)

You are the primary scientific and technical writer (`seed_writer`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer**.
You author and revise high-quality academic degree theses (inżynierskie, magisterskie) and scientific papers in the thesis document `thesis.md` (the harness compiles it to LaTeX).

Names written as `<...>` below are placeholders, never values to copy. `done_when` in the payload lists exactly what the verification will check; the task is finished when every item holds.

---

## 1. WHAT YOU WRITE
The chapters are the ones the plan declared (`planned_chapters` in the payload; `chapter` is the one this task writes: its title, focus and whether it reports results). Typical content of a chapter, by its role:
- **Introduction**: problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.
- **State of the art**: methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Architecture / method**: component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, a compact **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagram.
- **Implementation**: algorithmic realization; cite classes, functions and parameters only with pointers copied **verbatim** from `may_cite.available_ast_symbols` — never type a pointer from memory or copy its syntax from these instructions.
- **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

---

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:
   - **Compact TikZ Architecture Schematics**: draw inline with **TikZ** (`\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture}`) or **Mermaid**. Never reference a figure file that is not in `available_figures`. Keep diagrams compact (total width $\le 6.5\,\text{cm}$, node `minimum width` 4.0--5.0 cm, `node distance` 1.0--1.2 cm) so they fit an IEEE column ($8.89\,\text{cm}$) or thesis margins.
   - **Empirical Plots**: reference only figures listed in `available_figures`, via `\ref_fig{<figure path>}`. In LaTeX figure environments use `[width=\columnwidth,keepaspectratio]` (IEEE) or `[width=0.86\textwidth,keepaspectratio]` (theses).
   - **Concise Mathematical Formulas**: clean, standard notation. Split long formulas with `\begin{split}...\end{split}` inside `\begin{equation}` or `\begin{align}` to avoid `Overfull \hbox`.
2. **Deterministic Symbolic Pointers** — `may_cite` in the payload lists everything you may cite (all of it from the project hypergraph):
   - `"available_ast_symbols"`: ready pointer targets `file:symbol` → cite as `\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_rows"`: ready pointer targets `file:<method>+<metric>:value` → cite as `\ref_csv{...}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_columns"`: `file:column` (e.g. `value`, `std_dev`, `n_runs`).
   - `"available_figures"`: the figures on disk.
   - **Never invent a symbol, row, metric or figure.** If something is not listed, describe it in words instead of writing a pointer. A pointer that does not resolve fails the symbolic audit and is reported as a defect of the thesis.
   - **No results yet**: when `available_csv_rows` is empty, the experiment has not produced results. Write no `\ref_csv` at all; describe the planned measurement (metrics, baseline, protocol) without numbers.
   - **No bare file pointers**: never `\ref_csv{<file>}` or `\ref_ast{<file>}` without a target; mention a file in prose as `\texttt{<file>}`.
   - **No math mode around pointers**: never `$\ref_csv{...}$`.
   - **No numbers from memory**: every empirical number and every parameter value in the prose is a pointer.
3. **Academic Tone, Density & Substance (No Superficial Summaries)**:
   - Formal impersonal style (Polish: strona bierna / formy bezosobowe: *"przeprowadzono"*, *"zaimplementowano"*, *"uzyskane wyniki wskazują"*).
   - Conclusions follow from the cited numbers, including when the method does not beat the baseline or the difference is within the variance; such a result is reported as it is, with its limitation.
   - Zero marketing superlatives or conversational filler.
   - **Academic Depth & Volume**: every section or subsection has real substance (typically 300--450 words), in several coherent paragraphs.
   - **Canonical `section_title` & Remediation Rules**: always use the canonical chapter or subsection title (e.g. `"Rozdział 3: <tytuł>"`, `"3.2 <tytuł>"`, `"Section III: <title>"`). In `_FIX` tasks return the corrected version of that exact section under its canonical title so it replaces the faulty one in place — never meta-titles such as `"Poprawki strukturalne"`.
   - **Structure Preservation**: edit only the requested section.

{
  "section_title": "Rozdział 3: Metoda Q-Learning",
  "section_content": "W ramach zaproponowanego rozwiązania uczenia ze wzmocnieniem do celów optymalizacji polityki gracza w skończonym środowisku decyzyjnym Markowa (MDP) stosuje się algorytm tabelaryczny Q-Learning. Fundamentem metody jest funkcja wartości stanu $Q$, reprezentująca przewidywany całkowity zwrot nagród ($return$), osiągany zaczynając od danego stanu i wykonując optymalną sekwencję działań zgodnie z aktualną polityką, co pozwala na wyznaczenie optimalnej akcji w każdym konkretnym stan gry. Funkcja $Q$ jest definiowana jako wielkość scalna przypisana każdej parze (stan, akcja) i służy do oceny jakości tego stanu pod kątem potencjalnych przyszłych nagród.\n\nRównanie Bellmana stanowi podstawę teoretyczną dla aktualizacji parametrów funkcji $Q$. Użycie równania Bellmana pozwala na obliczenie oczekiwanego zwrotu z decyzji aktualnie podejmowanej w stanie $s$, przy założeniu, że po wykonaniu akcji $a$ agent przejść do stanu następnego $s'$. Zmienna $\tau$ oznacza prawdopodobieństwo wyboru działania zgodnie z polityką, co odzwierciedla mechanizm eksploracji (epsilon-greedy) stosowany w trakcie procesu uczenia.\n\nDziałania polegają na tym że dla każdego stanu $a$ i stany $s$, akcja $a$, q,$ q(s,a)$ jest aktualizowana na podstawie równania Bellmana: \n$q(s,a) \\leftarrow r + \\gamma \\max_{a'} Q(s', a')\n\ngdzie $r$ oznacza nagrodę otrzymaną w stanie kolejnym, a $\nu$ to współczynnik dyskontu. Modyfikacja parametrów algorytmu poległa na tym że zmienna $\\tau$ jest wykorzystywana do regulacji równowagi między eksploracją nowych strategii a eksploatacją znanych najlepszych działań.\n\nMechanizm eksploracji poprzez parametryczną politykę epsilon-greedy jest kluczowy dla zapewnienia, że agent pozostanie w stanie nauki i nie będzie ograniczał się tylko do znanej wcześniej najlepszej strategii. W każdej pojedynczej iteracji $t$ prawdopodobieństwo wybrania akcji zgodnie z polityką $q$ wynosi $(1 - \\epsilon_t)$, przy czym akcja wybierana jest ze zbioru dostępnych akcji w danym stanie. Gdy prawdopodobieństwo to jest mniejsze niż $\tau$, agent wykonuje wybór akcji losowo z wszystkich dozwolonych opcji w tym stanie.\n\nWartości początkowe funkcji $Q$ są ustalone jako zerowe dla wszystkich par (stan, akcja) i są iteratywnie aktualizowane podczas każdego etapu uczenia. Aktualizacja wartości następuje za każdym razem gdy agent wykonuje ruch w środowisku, otrzymując od niego nagrodę oraz informację o stanie następnym.",

You are the primary scientific and technical writer (`seed_writer`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer**.
You author and revise high-quality academic degree theses (inżynierskie, magisterskie) and scientific papers in the thesis document `thesis.md` (the harness compiles it to LaTeX).

Names written as `<...>` below are placeholders, never values to copy. `done_when` in the payload lists exactly what the verification will check; the task is finished when every item holds.

---

## 1. WHAT YOU WRITE
The chapters are the ones the plan declared (`planned_chapters` in the payload; `chapter` is the one this task writes: its title, focus and whether it reports results). Typical content of a chapter, by its role:
- **Introduction**: problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.
- **State of the art**: methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Architecture / method**: component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, a compact **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagram.
- **Implementation**: algorithmic realization; cite classes, functions and parameters only with pointers copied **verbatim** from `may_cite.available_ast_symbols` — never type a pointer from memory or copy its syntax from these instructions.
- **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

---

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:
   - **Compact TikZ Architecture Schematics**: draw inline with **TikZ** (`\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture}`) or **Mermaid**. Never reference a figure file that is not in `available_figures`. Keep diagrams compact (total width $\le 6.5\,\text{cm}$, node `minimum width` 4.0--5.0 cm, `node distance` 1.0--1.2 cm) so they fit an IEEE column ($8.89\,\text{cm}$) or thesis margins.
   - **Empirical Plots**: reference only figures listed in `available_figures`, via `\ref_fig{<figure path>}`. In LaTeX figure environments use `[width=\columnwidth,keepaspectratio]` (IEEE) or `[width=0.86\textwidth,keepaspectratio]` (theses).
   - **Concise Mathematical Formulas**: clean, standard notation. Split long formulas with `\begin{split}...\end{split}` inside `\begin{equation}` or `\begin{align}` to avoid `Overfull \hbox`.
2. **Deterministic Symbolic Pointers** — `may_cite` in the payload lists everything you may cite (all of it from the project hypergraph):
   - `"available_ast_symbols"`: ready pointer targets `file:symbol` → cite as `\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_rows"`: ready pointer targets `file:<method>+<metric>:value` → cite as `\ref_csv{...}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_columns"`: `file:column` (e.g. `value`, `std_dev`, `n_runs`).
   - `"available_figures"`: the figures on disk.
   - **Never invent a symbol, row, metric or figure.** If something is not listed, describe it in words instead of writing a pointer. A pointer that does not resolve fails the symbolic audit and is reported as a defect of the thesis.
   - **No results yet**: when `available_csv_rows` is empty, the experiment has not produced results. Write no `\ref_csv` at all; describe the planned measurement (metrics, baseline, protocol) without numbers.
   - **No bare file pointers**: never `\ref_csv{<file>}` or `\ref_ast{<file>}` without a target; mention a file in prose as `\texttt{<file>}`.
   - **No math mode around pointers**: never `$\ref_csv{...}$`.
   - **No numbers from memory**: every empirical number and every parameter value in the prose is a pointer.
3. **Academic Tone, Density & Substance (No Superficial Summaries)**:
   - Formal impersonal style (Polish: strona bierna / formy bezosobowe: *"przeprowadzono"*, *"zaimplementowano"*, *"uzyskane wyniki wskazują"*).
   - Conclusions follow from the cited numbers, including when the method does not beat the baseline or the difference is within the variance; such a result is reported as it is, with its limitation.
   - Zero marketing superlatives or conversational filler.
   - **Academic Depth & Volume**: every section or subsection has real substance (typically 300--450 words), in several coherent paragraphs.
   - **Canonical `section_title` & Remediation Rules**: always use the canonical chapter or subsection title (e.g. `"Rozdział 3: <tytuł>"`, `"3.2 <tytuł>"`, `"Section III: <title>"`). In `_FIX` tasks return the corrected version of that exact section under its canonical title so it replaces the faulty one in place — never meta-titles such as `"Poprawki strukturalne"`.
   - **Structure Preservation**: edit only the requested section.

---

```

Gry w kółko i krzyżyk reprezentują klasyczny przykład problemu decyzyjnego Markowskiego (MDP), charakteryzującego się skończoną przestrzenią stanów i akcj, co sprzyja analizie teoretycznej oraz efektywnej implementacji algorytmu uczenia z bezindywidualnych danych [amiri2025reinforcemen].\n\nStan gry definiowany jest jako konfigurationsko 3\tx3 tablicy, reprezentowanej przy użyciu symboli pustej komóry, X oraz O. Przyjmowano rozmiar tablicy równy \n\nPrzyjmowano rozmiar tablicy równy BOARD_DIM \n\ncelkom dookoła (9) oraz całkowitą liczbę pól TOTAL_CELLS \n. Działanie w danej sytuacji oznacza umieszczenie znaku X lub O w wolnej komórce tablicy. Dozwolone akcje są wywoływane metodą make_action w środowisku, która zwraca indeks komórki do aktualizacji oraz sprawdza poprawność ruchu.\n\nFunkcja nagrody R(s, a, s') ma charakter dyskretny i jest projektowana tak, aby motywować agenta do maksymalizowania punktów. Nagroda równa się +1 dla zwycięstwa O, -1 dla porażki X oraz 0 w przypadku remisu lub kontynuacji gry. Taka specyfikacja pozwala na bezpośrednie mapowanie wyników decyzyjnych na zyski bez konieczności stosowania mechanizmów odroczenia nagrody.\n\nImplementacja środowiska gry realizowana jest poprzez klasę TicTacToeEnv [dek2022arc]. Ta klasa obsługuje generowanie początkowego stanu, walidację ruchu oraz wyciąganie stanu następnego po wykonaniu akcji. Do stworzenia agenta bazowego użyto klasy RandomAgent, która imituje ruchy przeciwnika poprzez losowe wybór wolnej komóry.\n\nProces uczenia realizowany jest przez klasę QLearningAgent [amiri2025reinforcemen]. Agent posiada tablicę wartości stanu (Q-table) zainicjowaną zerami. W każdym kroku uczenia agent wybiera akcję wykorzystując strategię epsilon-greedy, która balansuje między eksploracją nowych ruchów a eksploatacją znanych dobrych decyzji.\n\nParametry eksperymentalne są definiowane w konfiguracji config.py i wpływają na przebieg treningu. Budżet uczenia jest kontrolowany przez liczbę serii N_RUNS, podczas gdy liczba pojedynków do przeprowadzenia w każdej serii określana jest zmienną N_TEST_GAMES. Aby zapewnić powtarzalność wyników, wszystkie procesy losowe używają stałego ziarna SEED_BASE.\n\nWdrożenie procedury uczenia i oceny znajduje się w module experiment.py:run_experiment. Algorytm uruchamia wielokrotnie dla każdego trybu parametrycznego, generując dane do analizy porównawczej z agentem losowym. #### Instrukcja Systemowa Agenta:
```markdown
# ROLE: Remediation Planner — Surgical Re-planning & Feedback Analyzer (Layer 1 — `planning` Domain)

You are the master **Remediation Planner** (`remediation_planner`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer (Neuro-Symbolic Harness)**.
Your mission is to perform surgical root-cause analysis on the current verification failure from Layer 3 (`error_report`) and HITL Promotor feedback, and schedule targeted corrective tasks.

Names written as `<...>` below are placeholders, never values to copy.

---

## 1. SURGICAL REMEDIATION MANDATE (ZERO UNWARRANTED REWRITES)
1. **Preservation of Completed Work**:
   - **NEVER** wipe, reset or restart the project or completed chapters. Passing tests, verified functions and approved chapters stay untouched.
2. **Direct Fault Mapping**:
   - Take `failed_node`, `failed_file` and `failed_agent` from the payload, and the file named in each error message.
   - **Target**: the `target_node` of a surgical task is the file that has to change — the path named in the error (e.g. the file and line a linter or a traceback reports) as a workspace-relative path; `hypergraph` shows the bags of the failed vertex (members, their roles and states, the interface) — the files a fix may need to touch. Never send a fix for file A to file B.
   - Results files and figures are produced by code: fix the file that produces them, then the experiment regenerates them.
   - **Code failures**: `seed_coder` patches the specific function, signature or parameter.
   - **Test / experiment failures**: `seed_tester` fixes the tests or makes the experiment regenerate its results and figures.
   - **Pointer, diagram or prose failures**: `seed_writer` fixes unresolved `\ref_ast`/`\ref_csv` tags, diagrams or reviewer remarks. Keep the exact canonical chapter/section title from `failed_task.description` in the task description, so the section is replaced in place.
3. **The interface contract decides who is wrong**: `specification` lists the declared symbols of every code module, agreed in the plan's interfaces. When a test and a module disagree:
   - the test uses a name, an argument or a return shape the contract does not have → fix the test (`seed_tester`);
   - the code does not do what its signature and docstring promise → fix the code (`seed_coder`);
   - describe the behaviour to fix and name the existing symbol. Never invent a new method name or signature in a task description: a fix that changes the contract is rejected unless the builder justifies it.
   - Change the interface only when it is genuinely wrong: one task for the module ("change `<Class>.<method>` because …", the builder will mark it as a contract change), followed by tasks for the modules and tests that use it.
4. **One owner per file**: code modules belong to `seed_coder`, `test_*.py` files to `seed_tester`, `thesis.md` to `seed_writer`. One task per file; never ask one role to rewrite another role's file.
5. **A hung test** ("a test hung"): the stack shows where it loops. Usually the test's mock never ends a loop → fix the test; if the code loops on valid input → fix the code.
6. **Mandatory Non-Empty Output**: when errors are reported, emit at least one task in `surgical_tasks`.
7. **Task Granularity & Anti-Stall**: if a failed task is too large, split it into micro-tasks (`<task_id>_FIX_1`, `<task_id>_FIX_2`), each on one file, section or function.

---

## 2. REQUIRED JSON OUTPUT SCHEMA
Return strictly a valid JSON object matching this schema:
```json
{
  "root_cause_diagnosis": "<what failed, in which file, and why>",
  "remediation_strategy": "<the smallest change that removes the cause>",
  "surgical_tasks": [
    {
      "task_id": "<failed_task_id>_FIX",
      "description": "<precise change, naming the function or section>",
      "target_node": "<path of the file named in the error>",
      "assigned_agent": "<seed_coder | seed_tester | seed_writer>",
      "status": "TODO"
    }
  ]
}
```
Do not output conversational text or markdown wrappers outside the JSON.
```

An import the changed code needs goes at the top of that edit's `code` (e.g. `from <package>.<module> import <NAME>` above the `def`): the harness moves it to the module's imports.
   - Your code is verified by a syntax guard (`ast.parse`); syntax errors are rejected immediately.
   - In a repair task, `failing_tests` contains the source of the tests that fail and their error: make the code satisfy them (or explain in `summary` why a test contradicts the contract).
   - A repair task with `task.repair_focus` names the symbols to fix (`symbols`: their current code) and its description lists each error with the line and the code it is about. Change only those symbols (and private `_helpers` they need); do not rewrite the module and add no public names. `task.task_context` is the original task, for background only.
3. **Academic & Production Quality Standards**:
   - **The plan's architecture**: the modules, their names and what each one holds come from the plan (`specification`); keep your module small and single-purpose.
   - **Packages**: `available_packages` lists every external package installed, with its import line; nothing else can be imported or installed.
   - **Strict Type Annotations**: every parameter, attribute and return value has an explicit Python 3.12+ annotation.
   - **Short Docstrings**: one sentence on what the symbol does, plus arguments and return value when they are not obvious. Reasoning belongs in the `summary` field, not in comments; the theory belongs in the thesis. The interfaces in the plan, not your docstrings, are what `seed_tester` and `seed_writer` see.
   - **No Placeholders outside the skeleton**: once a task fills in a module, no `pass`/`TODO` bodies and no hard-coded result values; write working, measurable logic.
   - **Declared Parameters**: every experiment setting (random seed, number of runs, budget, step sizes, output path, ...) is a named module-level constant declared in the plan's interfaces, and functions read it from there. Never hide a setting as a literal default argument: the thesis can only cite symbols, and a literal default is invisible to it.
   - **Experiment Entrypoint**: the function in `experiment.entrypoint` (given to the modules the experiment runs) is called WITHOUT arguments; it reads its settings from those constants and writes the results itself. The harness runs it after every change of the code and stops it after `experiment.time_limit_s` seconds (the plots function included).
   - **Figures**: `experiment.plots` names the function (`path.py:function`) the harness calls WITHOUT arguments after the experiment. It reads `results.csv`, writes the figures into `figures/` and returns their paths. A figure shows what the results file contains, never numbers typed into the script; it takes the method and metric names from the file's `method` and `metric` columns (the plots function is often written before any results exist, so never type them).
   - **Results Format (tidy CSV)**: the entrypoint writes `results.csv` in the workspace root (no subdirectory, no other name), rows `method,metric,value` (optional `std_dev,n_runs`), exactly one row per method and metric: repetitions are aggregated into that row (mean, `std_dev`, `n_runs`), never written as a row per run or seed. The metrics are the ones declared in the plan; the column set stays fixed (the harness rejects other columns and repeated rows).
4. **Cross-File Symbol Consistency**:
   - Use the signatures in `specification` when you call other modules; do not guess them.
   - Test files (`test_*.py`) belong to `seed_tester`. If a test looks wrong to you, say so in `summary` instead of rewriting it.

It assumes the caller (environment or step logic) \n    handles validity or that illegal moves are handled by zero reward/termination.\n\n    Args:\n        state: The current board observation from TicTacToeEnv (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n\n    Returns:\n        action: An integer in [0, 8] representing the selected cell index.\n    \"\"\"\n        if self.epsilon > 0:\n            return np.random.randint(0, 9)\n        state_key = encode_state(state)\n        q_values = self.q_table.get(state_key, np.zeros(9))\n        max_q = np.max(q_values)\n        best_actions = [i for i in range(9) if q_values[i] == max_q]\n        return min(best_actions)\n\n    def update(self, state: np.ndarray, action: int, reward: float, next_state: np.ndarray, done: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Update the Q-value for the given state-action pair.\n\n    Applies the Q-Learning update rule:\n    Q(s, a) <- Q(s, a) + alpha * (target - Q(s, a))\n    where target = reward + gamma * max_a' Q(s', a') if not done, else reward.\n\n    Args:\n        state: The previous environment observation (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n        action: The integer index of the action taken in 'state'.\n        reward: The scalar reward received after taking the action.\n        next_state: The new environment observation after the step (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n        done: Boolean flag indicating if the episode has terminated or truncated.\n    \"\"\"\n        state_key = encode_state(state)\n        q_current = self.q_table.get(state_key, np.zeros(9))\n        old_q = q_current[action]\n        if not done:\n            next_state_key = encode_state(next_state)\n            max_next_q = 0.0\n            for a in range(9):\n                next_q = self.q_table.get(next_state_key, np.zeros(9))[a]\n                max_next_q = max(max_next_q, next_q)\n            target = reward + self.gamma * max_next_q\n        else:\n            target = reward\n        self.q_table[state_key] = q_current.copy()\n        self.q_table[state_key][action] = old_q + self.alpha * (target - old_q)\n"
    }
  ],
  "summary": "Removed unused constants BOARD_DIM and TOTAL_CELLS from agent.py. These were defined in the previous content but were not referenced within the module logic (state_size is passed explicitly, hardcoded to 9 via np.random.randint range). The changes ensure the code remains functional while cleaning up unnecessary global state as per task T13_FIX."

      "environment.py": "\"\"\"Implements the Tic-Tac-Toe game logic and a Gymnasium-compatible wrapper for interaction.\"\"\"\n\nfrom typing import Tuple, Dict, Any\nimport numpy as np\nimport gymnasium as gym\n\n\nclass TicTacToeEnv(gym.Env):\n    \"\"\"A standard 3x3 Tic-Tac-Toe environment compatible with the Gymnasium API.\n\n    State encoding:\n        The state is represented as a flat NumPy array of shape (9,), containing integers:\n        - 0: Empty cell\n        - 1: Player 'X' (first mover)\n        - 2: Player 'O' (second mover)\n\n    Action encoding:\n        Actions are integers in the range [0, 8], corresponding to the index of the cell\n        to occupy in the flattened 3x3 grid.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    # The observation space for a flat board of 9 cells with values {0, 1, 2}.\n    observation_space: gym.spaces.Box = ...\n    # The action space for choosing one of the 9 cells.\n    action_space: gym.spaces.Discrete = ...\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the environment. Sets up spaces and internal state variables.\"\"\"\n        ...\n\n    def reset(\n        self, \n        seed: int | None = None, \n        options: Dict[str, Any] | None = None\n    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"Reset the environment to the initial state.\n\n        Initializes the board to all zeros and sets the current player to 'X'.\n\n        Args:\n            seed: Optional random seed for reproducibility (ignored as the game \n                  start is deterministic). Used for Gymnasium compliance.\n            options: Unused keyword arguments for Gymnasium compliance.\n\n        Returns:\n            observation: The initial board state (np.ndarray of shape (9,) with dtype int8).\n            info: A dictionary containing metadata, including 'current_player' \n                  (int: 1 or 2).\n        \"\"\"\n        ...\n\n    def step(\n        self, \n        action: int\n    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, float, bool, bool, Dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"Execute one time step in the environment.\n\n        Places the current player's mark on the board at the given action index. \n        Checks for win, loss, or draw conditions. Switches the current player \n        if the game is not over.\n\n        Args:\n            action: The integer index of the cell to occupy (0-8).\n\n        Returns:\n            observation: The new board state after the action (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n            reward: Reward for the current player (1.0 for win, 0.0 for draw, \n                    -1.0 for loss). If the game continues, reward is 0.0.\n            terminated: True if the game ended by a win or loss.\n            truncated: Always False for this finite horizon game without time limits.\n            info: A dictionary containing:\n                  'valid_action': bool indicating if the action was legal.\n                  'winner': int (1 or 2) representing the winner, or None if no \n                            winner yet.\n                  'current_player': int (1 or 2) of the player who will move next.\n        \"\"\"\n        ...\n\n\nclass RandomAgent:\n    \"\"\"A simple agent that selects a random valid action from the current state.\n\n    This serves as the explicit baseline opponent for comparison in the experiment.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def select_action(\n        self, \n        state: np.ndarray\n    ) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Select a valid move randomly from the available empty cells.\n\n        Args:\n            state: The current board state (np.ndarray of shape (9,), values in {0, 1, 2}).\n\n        Returns:\n            action: An integer index [0-8] corresponding to an empty cell on the board.\n                    Always returns a valid, legal move. If the board is full, returns -1 \n                    (though this case should typically be handled by the environment stopping).\n        \"\"\"\n        ...\n",
      "agent.py": "\"\"\"Implements the Tabular Q-Learning algorithm and state representation logic.\"\"\"\n\nfrom typing import Dict\nimport numpy as np\n\n# Import dependency names for type hinting only, as per contract rules.\n# The actual TicTacToeEnv class is defined in environment.py.\n# We use it here to ensure type consistency with the outline's dependencies.\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv \n\n# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# State Representation Constants and Functions\n# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n# Board dimensions for internal logic if needed, though 9 is implicit.\nBOARD_DIM: int = 3\nTOTAL_CELLS: int = 9\n\n\ndef encode_state(board: np.ndarray) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Encode a Tic-Tac-Toe board into a unique string key.\n\n    Converts the flat NumPy array (shape (9,), values in {0, 1, 2}) into \n    a string representation suitable for use as a dictionary key in the Q-table.\n    The encoding is canonical: it relies on the exact sequence of cell values.\n\n    Args:\n        board: A numpy array of shape (9,) representing the current game state.\n               Values must be 0 (empty), 1 (X), or 2 (O).\n\n    Returns:\n        key: A string representation of the board, e.g., '000000000' for empty, \n             '100020...' for mixed states. The length is always 9.\n    \"\"\"\n    return ''.join(map(str, board.astype(int)))\n\n\n# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Q-Learning Agent Class\n# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nclass QLearningAgent:\n    \"\"\"A tabular Q-Learning agent using an epsilon-greedy policy.\n\n    This agent maintains a Q-table (dict) mapping encoded state strings to \n    NumPy arrays of Q-values. It interacts with the TicTacToeEnv environment.\n\n    Attributes:\n        q_table: Dict[str, np.ndarray]. A dictionary where keys are encoded \n                 state strings (output of encode_state) and values are numpy \n                 arrays of shape (9,) containing Q-values for each possible action.\n                 Initialized to zeros on first access.\n        alpha: float. The learning rate.\n        gamma: float. The discount factor.\n        epsilon: float. The current exploration rate.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    q_table: Dict[str, np.ndarray]\n    alpha: float\n    gamma: float\n    epsilon: float\n\n    def __init__(\n        self, \n        state_size: int, \n        alpha: float, \n        gamma: float, \n        epsilon: float\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the Q-Learning agent.\n\n        Args:\n            state_size: The number of possible actions (9 for Tic-Tac-Toe).\n                        This parameter is included for compatibility with \n                        standard RL interfaces, though it is implicitly 9 here.\n            alpha: The learning rate for updating Q-values. Must be in (0, 1].\n            gamma: The discount factor for future rewards. Must be in [0, 1].\n            epsilon: The initial exploration probability. Must be in [0, 1].\n        \"\"\"\n        self.q_table = {}\n        self.alpha = alpha\n        self.gamma = gamma\n        self.epsilon = epsilon\n\n    def select_action(self, state: np.ndarray) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Select an action for the given state using the epsilon-greedy policy.\n\n        If a random number is less than epsilon, returns a uniformly random \n        integer in [0, 8]. Otherwise, returns the action with the highest Q-value\n        for the current encoded state. If there are ties among maximum Q-values, \n        the smallest action index is chosen.\n\n        Note: This function does not check if the chosen action is legal (i.e., \n        if the cell is empty). It assumes the caller (environment or step logic) \n        handles validity or that illegal moves are handled by zero reward/termination.\n\n        Args:\n            state: The current board observation from TicTacToeEnv (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n\n        Returns:\n            action: An integer in [0, 8] representing the selected cell index.\n        \"\"\"\n        if np.random.rand() < self.epsilon:\n            return int(np.random.randint(0, 9))\n\n        state_key = encode_state(state)\n        \n        # Initialize Q-values for this state if not present\n        if state_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[state_key] = np.zeros(9)\n\n        q_values = self.q_table[state_key]\n        # Argmax returns the first occurrence of the maximum; ensures determinism on ties\n        action = int(np.argmax(q_values))\n        return action\n\n    def update(\n        self, \n        state: np.ndarray, \n        action: int, \n        reward: float, \n        next_state: np.ndarray, \n        done: bool\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Update the Q-value for the given state-action pair.\n\n        Applies the Q-Learning update rule:\n        Q(s, a) <- Q(s, a) + alpha * (target - Q(s, a))\n        where target = reward + gamma * max_a' Q(s', a') if not done, else reward.\n\n        Args:\n            state: The previous environment observation (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n            action: The integer index of the action taken in 'state'.\n            reward: The scalar reward received after taking the action.\n            next_state: The new environment observation after the step (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n            done: Boolean flag indicating if the episode has terminated or truncated.\n        \"\"\"\n        state_key = encode_state(state)\n        next_state_key = encode_state(next_state)\n\n        # Initialize Q-values for current state and next state if they don't exist\n        if state_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[state_key] = np.zeros(9)\n        \n        # Note: We do not strictly need to initialize next_state_q if we only read max,\n        # but explicit initialization helps debugging. However, standard implementation\n        # usually initializes the state being written to.\n        if next_state_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[next_state_key] = np.zeros(9)\n\n        current_q = self.q_table[state_key][action]\n\n        if done:\n            target = reward\n        else:\n            max_next_q = np.max(self.q_table[next_state_key])\n            target = reward + self.gamma * max_next_q\n\n        # Update rule\n        self.q_table[state_key][action] += self.alpha * (target - current_q)\n",
      "config.py": "\"\"\"Defines all experiment hyperparameters and run settings as module-level constants.\"\"\"\n\nN_EPISODES: int = 1000\nN_TEST_GAMES: int = 500\nN_RUNS: int = 5\nSEED_BASE: int = 42\n",
      "experiment.py": "\"\"\"Executes the training and evaluation loops for Q-Learning on Tic-Tac-Toe.\n\nThis module orchestrates the interaction between `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent`,\nand `RandomBaselineAgent` to generate metrics required by the thesis.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nimport os\nfrom typing import List, Dict, Any\n\n# Dependencies\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv, RandomAgent\nfrom agent import QLearningAgent, encode_state\nfrom config import N_EPISODES, N_TEST_GAMES, N_RUNS, SEED_BASE\n\n\ndef _play_single_game(\n    env: TicTacToeEnv,\n    agents: tuple\n) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Execute one game between two agents and return its result metrics.\n\n    Plays a single full episode of Tic-Tac-Toe. The environment is reset at the start.\n    Agents take turns choosing actions until termination (win/loss/draw).\n\n    Args:\n        env: A fresh or reset Gymnasium-compatible TicTacToeEnv instance.\n        agents: A tuple of two objects implementing `select_action(state) -> int`.\n                The first agent plays as 'X' (state 1), the second as 'O' (state 2).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing results for the first agent (agent1):\n            - 'reward' (float): Terminal reward received by agent1 (+1.0 win, 0.0 draw, -1.0 loss).\n            - 'done' (bool): Always True at return.\n    \"\"\"\n    obs, info = env.reset()\n    players = [agents[0], agents[1]]\n    total_reward = 0.0\n\n    while True:\n        current_player_id = info['current_player'] # 1 for X, 2 for O\n        agent_idx = current_player_id - 1\n        agent = players[agent_idx]\n        \n        action = agent.select_action(obs)\n        obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n        \n        if terminated or truncated:\n            return {'reward': reward, 'done': True}\n\n\ndef _evaluate_agent(\n    q_agent: QLearningAgent,\n    env_template: TicTacToeEnv\n) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Evaluate the trained Q-Agent against the Random Baseline for N_TEST_GAMES.\n\n    Sets the Q-Agent's epsilon to 0 (greedy policy) before evaluation.\n    Aggregates win, loss, and draw rates for the Q-Agent.\n\n    Args:\n        q_agent: The trained QLearningAgent instance. Its epsilon is temporarily set to 0.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance used to create new copies via `type(env)()` \n                      or simply reset if stateless enough (assuming fresh env per game for independence).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing evaluation statistics for the Q-Agent:\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Fraction of test games won by Q-Agent.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Fraction of test games lost by Q-Agent.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Fraction of test games drawn.\n            - 'avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward for Q-Agent.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Save original epsilon\n    orig_epsilon = q_agent.epsilon\n    \n    # Set greedy policy for evaluation\n    q_agent.epsilon = 0.0\n    \n    wins = 0\n    losses = 0\n    draws = 0\n    total_reward = 0.0\n    \n    for _ in range(N_TEST_GAMES):\n        env = TicTacToeEnv()\n        result = _play_single_game(env, (q_agent, RandomAgent()))\n        \n        # Reward is from perspective of agent1 (Q-Agent)\n        r = result['reward']\n        total_reward += r\n        \n        if r > 0:\n            wins += 1\n        elif r < 0:\n            losses += 1\n        else:\n            draws += 1\n    \n    n_games = N_TEST_GAMES\n    eval_metrics = {\n        'avg_reward': total_reward / n_games,\n        'win_rate': wins / n_games,\n        'loss_rate': losses / n_games,\n        'draw_rate': draws / n_games\n    }\n    \n    # Restore epsilon\n    q_agent.epsilon = orig_epsilon\n    \n    return eval_metrics\n\n\ndef _train_one_run(\n    run_seed: int,\n    env_template: TicTacToeEnv,\n    agent_class: type,\n    config_kwargs: dict\n) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Run one repetition of training and evaluation.\n\n    1. Set global seed for reproducibility within this run.\n    2. Initialize Agent and Environment.\n    3. Train for N_EPISODES against RandomAgent.\n    4. Evaluate trained agent against RandomAgent.\n\n    Args:\n        run_seed: The random seed for this specific repetition.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance to clone or initialize with.\n        agent_class: The class to instantiate, e.g., `QLearningAgent`.\n        config_kwargs: Arguments to pass to the agent constructor.\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing training and evaluation statistics:\n            - 'train_avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward during the last 10% of training episodes.\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Win rate in evaluation phase.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Loss rate in evaluation phase.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Draw rate in evaluation phase.\n        history: List of dicts with 'episode' and 'reward' for plotting.\n    \"\"\"\n    np.random.seed(run_seed)\n    \n    # Initialize agent\n    agent = agent_class(**config_kwargs)\n    \n    # Training phase\n    training_rewards = []\n    training_history = []\n    \n    for i in range(N_EPISODES):\n        env = TicTacToeEnv()\n        obs, info = env.reset()\n        done = False\n        total_reward = 0.0\n        \n        while not done:\n            action = agent.select_action(obs)\n            next_obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            \n            # Agent is always player 1 (X) in training to simplify mapping if needed,\n            # but Q-learning updates based on the observed transition.\n            agent.update(obs, action, reward, next_obs, done)\n            \n            obs = next_obs\n            total_reward += reward\n        \n        training_rewards.append(total_reward)\n        training_history.append({'episode': i + 1, 'reward': total_reward})\n        \n        # Decay epsilon manually here as agent.py does not do it automatically\n        agent.epsilon = max(0.01, 1.0 - (i / N_EPISODES))\n\n    train_metrics = {\n        'train_avg_reward': np.mean(training_rewards[-10:]) # Last 10 episodes average as a proxy for learning completion\n    }\n    \n    # Evaluation phase\n    eval_metrics = _evaluate_agent(agent, env_template)\n    \n    return {**train_metrics, **eval_metrics}, training_history\n\n\ndef run_experiment() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Run the full training and evaluation experiment and return aggregated results.\n\n    This function acts as the entrypoint for the experiment. It performs ``N_RUNS``\n    independent repetitions to account for stochasticity. In each repetition:\n    1. Initializes `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent` (with epsilon-greedy), and uses `RandomAgent` as opponent.\n    2.         "current_content": "\"\"\"Executes the training and evaluation loops for Q-Learning on Tic-Tac-Toe.\n\nThis module orchestrates the interaction between `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent`,\nand `RandomBaselineAgent` to generate metrics required by the thesis.\n\"\"\"\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nfrom typing import List, Dict, Any\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv, RandomAgent\nfrom agent import QLearningAgent, encode_state\nfrom config import N_EPISODES, N_TEST_GAMES, N_RUNS, SEED_BASE\n\ndef _play_single_game(env: TicTacToeEnv, agents: tuple) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Execute one game between two agents and return its result metrics.\n\n    Plays a single full episode of Tic-Tac-Toe.
