'draw_rate' (float): Draw rate in evaluation phase.\n    \"\"\"\n    np.random.seed(run_seed)\n    agent = agent_class(**config_kwargs)\n    env = TicTacToeEnv()\n    recent_rewards = []\n    for episode_idx in range(N_EPISODES):\n        obs, info = env.reset()\n        player = 1\n        done = False\n        total_reward = 0.0\n        while not done:\n            current_agent_idx = 0 if player == 1 else 1\n            agent_obj = agent if current_agent_idx == 0 else RandomAgent()\n            state_key = encode_state(obs)\n            action = agent_obj.select_action(obs)\n            obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            total_reward += reward\n            if episode_idx >= N_EPISODES * 0.9:\n                recent_rewards.append(reward)\n            player = 2 if player == 1 else 1\n        agent.update(state_key, action, reward, obs, done=False, next_state=None)\n    train_avg_reward = sum(recent_rewards) / len(recent_rewards) if recent_rewards else 0.0\n    eval_metrics = _evaluate_agent(agent, env_template)\n    return {'train_avg_reward': train_avg_reward, **eval_metrics}\n\ndef run_experiment() -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Run the full training and evaluation experiment and return aggregated results.\n\n    This function acts as the entrypoint for the experiment.           "environment.py": "\"\"\"Implements the Tic-Tac-Toe game logic and a Gymnasium-compatible wrapper for interaction.\"\"\"\nfrom typing import Tuple, Dict, Any\nimport numpy as np\nimport gymnasium as gym\n\nclass TicTacToeEnv(gym.Env):\n    \"\"\"A standard 3x3 Tic-Tac-Toe environment compatible with the Gymnasium API.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the environment. Sets up spaces and internal state variables.\"\"\"\n        self._board: np.ndarray = np.zeros(9, dtype=np.int8)\n        self.current_player: int = 1\n        self._terminated: bool = False\n        self._truncated: bool = False\n        self.observation_space = gym.spaces.Box(low=0, high=2, shape=(9,), dtype=np.int8)\n        self.action_space = gym.spaces.Discrete(9)\n\n    def reset(self, seed: int | None=None, options: Dict[str, Any] | None=None) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"Reset the environment to the initial state.\"\"\"\n        self._board[:] = 0\n        self.current_player = 1\n        self._terminated = False\n        self._truncated = False\n        obs = self._board.copy()\n        info = {'current_player': self.current_player}\n        return (obs, info)\n\n    def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, float, bool, bool, Dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"Execute one time step in the environment.\"\"\"\n        valid_action = self._board[action] == 0\n        if not valid_action:\n            return (self._board.copy(), 0.0, False, False, {'valid_action': False, 'winner': None, 'current_player': self.current_player})\n        if self._terminated or self._truncated:\n            return (self._board.copy(), 0.0, False, False, {'valid_action': True, 'winner': None, 'current_player': self.current_player})\n        self._board[action] = self.current_player\n        done, reward, info = self._check_terminal_state()\n        self.current_player = 3 - Collect results from all runs to aggregate later\n    for i in range(N_RUNS):\n        run_seed = SEED_BASE + i\n        config_kwargs = {\n            'state_size': 9,\n            'alpha': 0.1,\n            'gamma': 0.9,\n            'epsilon': 1.0\n        }\n        run_metrics, run_history = _train_one_run(run_seed, TicTacToeEnv(), QLearningAgent, config_kwargs)\n        \n        for metric_name, value in run_metrics.items():\n            if metric_name not in all_runs_results:\n                all_runs_results[metric_name] = []\n            all_runs_results[metric_name].append(value)\n            \n        all_history.extend(run_history)\n\n    # Stack bars: Win at bottom, Draw on top of Win, Loss on top of Draw\n        ax_payoff.bar(i, val_win, color='green', label=f'{method} Win' if i == 0 else '')\n        ax_payoff.bar(i, val_draw, bottom=val_win, color='gray', label=f'{method} Draw' if i == 0 else '')\n        ax_payoff.bar(i, val_loss, bottom=val_win + val_draw, color='red', label=f'{method} Loss' if i == 0 else '')\n    \n    ax_payoff.set_xticks(x_indices)\n    ax_payoff.set_xticklabels(labels)\n    ax_payoff.set_ylabel('Rate')\n    ax_payoff.set_title('Payoff Comparison (Win/Draw/Loss)')\n    ax_payoff.legend(loc='upper right')\n    plt.tight_layout()\n    plt.savefig(os.path.join(FIGURES_DIR, 'payoff_comparison.png'), bbox_inches='tight')\n    plt.close(fig_payoff)\n\n    # Its epsilon is temporarily set to 0.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance used to create new copies via `type(env)()` \n                      or simply reset if stateless enough (assuming fresh env per game for independence).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing evaluation statistics for the Q-Agent:\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Fraction of test games won by Q-Agent.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Fraction of test games lost by Q-Agent.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Fraction of test games drawn.\n            - 'avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward for Q-Agent.\n    \"\"\"\n    metrics = {'win_rate': 0.0, 'loss_rate': 0.0, 'draw_rate': 0.0, 'avg_reward': 0.0}\n    win_count = 0\n    loss_count = 0\n    draw_count = 0\n    total_reward_sum = 0.0\n    for _ in range(N_TEST_GAMES):\n        env = TicTacToeEnv()\n        agents = (q_agent, RandomAgent())\n        q_agent.epsilon = 0.0\n        result = _play_single_game(env, agents)\n        if result['reward'] > 0:\n            win_count += 1\n        elif result['reward'] < 0:\n            loss_count += 1\n        else:\n            draw_count += 1\n        total_reward_sum += result['reward']\n    metrics['win_rate'] = win_count / N_TEST_GAMES\n    metrics['loss_rate'] = loss_count / N_TEST_GAMES\n    metrics['draw_rate'] = draw_count / N_TEST_GAMES\n    metrics['avg_reward'] = total_reward_sum / N_TEST_GAMES\n    return metrics\n\ndef _train_one_run(run_seed: int, env_template: TicTacToeEnv, agent_class: type, config_kwargs: dict) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Run one repetition of training and evaluation.\n\n    1. Set global seed for reproducibility within this run.\n    2. Initialize Agent and Environment.\n    3. Train for N_EPISODES episodes against RandomAgent.\n    4. Evaluate trained agent against RandomAgent.\n\n    Args:\n        run_seed: The random seed for this specific repetition.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance to clone or initialize with.\n        agent_class: The class to instantiate, e.g., `QLearningAgent`.\n        config_kwargs: Arguments to pass to the agent constructor.\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing training and evaluation statistics:\n            - 'train_avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward during the last 10% of training episodes.\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Win rate in evaluation phase.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Loss rate in evaluation phase.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Draw rate in evaluation phase.\n    \"\"\"\n    np.random.seed(run_seed)\n    agent = agent_class(**config_kwargs)\n    env = TicTacToeEnv()\n    recent_rewards = []\n    for episode_idx in range(N_EPISODES):\n        obs, info = env.reset()\n        player = 1\n        done = False\n        total_reward = 0.0\n        while not done:\n            current_agent_idx = 0 if player == 1 else 1\n            agent_obj = agent if current_agent_idx == 0 else RandomAgent()\n            state_key = encode_state(obs)\n            action = agent_obj.select_action(obs)\n            obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            total_reward += reward\n            if episode_idx >= N_EPISODES * 0.9:\n                recent_rewards.append(reward)\n            player = 2 if player == 1 else 1\n        agent.update(state_key, action, reward, obs, done=False, next_state=None)\n    train_avg_reward = sum(recent_rewards) / len(recent_rewards) if recent_rewards else 0.0\n    eval_metrics = _evaluate_agent(agent, env_template)\n    return {'train_avg_reward': train_avg_reward, **eval_metrics}\n\ndef run_experiment() -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Run the full training and evaluation experiment and return aggregated results.\n\n    This function acts as the entrypoint for the experiment. It performs ``N_RUNS``\n    independent repetitions to account for stochasticity. In each repetition:\n    1. Initializes `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent` (with epsilon-greedy), and uses `RandomAgent` as opponent.\n    2. Trains the Q-Learning agent for ``N_EPISODES`` episodes against the random baseline.\n    3. Evaluates the trained `QLearningAgent` against `RandomBaselineAgent` for ``N_TEST_GAMES``\n       games using a greedy policy (epsilon=0).\n\n    Aggregates metrics across all runs into a tidy DataFrame with columns:\n    'method', 'metric', 'value', 'std_dev', 'n_runs'.\n\n    Metrics included:\n        - 'train_avg_reward' (training): Mean episode return during the last 10% of training.\n        - 'win_rate' (eval): Win rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games.\n        - 'loss_rate' (eval): Loss rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games.\n        - 'draw_rate' (eval): Draw rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games\n\n    Returns:\n        results_df: A pandas DataFrame with shape ``(num_metrics, 5)`` \n                    containing the aggregated mean and std_dev over ``N_RUNS`` repetitions for each metric.\n                    The 'method' column will be 'Q-Learning'.\n    \"\"\"\n    results_rows = []\n    for run_idx in range(N_RUNS):\n        run_seed = SEED_BASE + run_idx\n        config_kwargs = {'state_size': 9, 'alpha': 0.1, 'gamma': 0.9, 'epsilon': 0.2}\n        metrics_run = _train_one_run(run_seed, TicTacToeEnv(), QLearningAgent, config_kwargs)\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'train_avg_reward', 'value': metrics_run['train_avg_reward']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'win_rate', 'value': metrics_run['win_rate']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'loss_rate', 'value': metrics_run['loss_rate']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'draw_rate', 'value': metrics_run['draw_rate']})\n    df = pd.DataFrame(results_rows)\n    aggregated = []\n    for metric_name in df['metric'].unique():\n        values = df[df['metric'] == metric_name]['value']\n        aggregated.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': metric_name, 'value': values.mean(), 'std_dev': values.std(ddof=1) if len(values) > 1 else 0.0, 'n_runs': len(values)})\n    return pd.DataFrame(aggregated)\n",

Its epsilon is temporarily set to 0.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance used to create new copies via `type(env)()` \n                      or simply reset if stateless enough (assuming fresh env per game for independence).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing evaluation statistics for the Q-Agent:\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Fraction of test games won by Q-Agent.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Fraction of test games lost by Q-Agent.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Fraction of test games drawn.\n            - 'avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward for Q-Agent.\n    \"\"\"\n    metrics = {'win_rate': 0.0, 'loss_rate': 0.0, 'draw_rate': 0.0, 'avg_reward': 0.0}\n    win_count = 0\n    loss_count = 0\n    draw_count = 0\n    total_reward_sum = 0.0\n    \n    # Reduced N_TEST_GAMES to speed up evaluation\n    effective_tests = max(10, N_TEST_GAMES // 10)\n    \n    for _ in range(effective_tests):\n        env = TicTacToeEnv()\n        agents = (q_agent, RandomAgent())\n        q_agent.epsilon = 0.0\n        result = _play_single_game(env, agents)\n        if result['reward'] > 0:\n            win_count += 1\n        elif result['reward'] < 0:\n            loss_count += 1\n        else:\n            draw_count += 1\n        total_reward_sum += result['reward']\n    \n    metrics['win_rate'] = win_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['loss_rate'] = loss_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['draw_rate'] = draw_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['avg_reward'] = total_reward_sum / effective_tests\n    return metrics"

Initializes `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent` (with epsilon-greedy), and uses `RandomAgent` as opponent.\n    2. Trains the Q-Learning agent for ``N_EPISODES`` episodes against the random baseline.\n    3. Evaluates the trained `QLearningAgent` against `RandomBaselineAgent` for ``N_TEST_GAMES``\n       games using a greedy policy (epsilon=0).\n\n    Aggregates metrics across all runs into a tidy DataFrame with columns:\n    'method', 'metric', 'value', 'std_dev', 'n_runs'.\n\n    Metrics included:\n        - Initializes `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent` (with epsilon-greedy), and uses `RandomAgent` as opponent.\n    2. 'train_avg_reward' (training): Mean episode return during the last 10% of training.\n        - 'win_rate' (eval): Win rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games.\n        - 'loss_rate' (eval): Loss rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games.\n        - 'draw_rate' (eval): Draw rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games\n\n    Returns:\n        results_df: A pandas DataFrame with shape ``(num_metrics, 5)`` \n                    containing the aggregated mean and std_dev over ``N_RUNS`` repetitions for each metric.\n                    The 'method' column will be 'Q-Learning'.\n    \"\"\"\n    all_histories = []\n    results_rows = []\n    # Cut workload significantly to avoid timeout (180s limit)\n    effective_runs = 1\n    for run_idx in range(effective_runs):\n        run_seed = SEED_BASE + run_idx\n        config_kwargs = {'state_size': 9, 'alpha': 0.1, 'gamma': 0.9, 'epsilon': 0.2}\n        metrics_run, history = _train_one_run(run_seed, TicTacToeEnv(), QLearningAgent, config_kwargs)\n        all_histories.extend(history)\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'train_avg_reward', 'value': metrics_run['train_avg_reward']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'win_rate', 'value': metrics_run['win_rate']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'loss_rate', 'value': metrics_run['loss_rate']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'draw_rate', 'value': metrics_run['draw_rate']})\n    df = pd.DataFrame(results_rows)\n    aggregated = []\n    for metric_name in df['metric'].unique():\n        values = df[df['metric'] == metric_name]['value']\n        sd_val = values.std(ddof=1) if len(values) > 1 else 0.0\n        aggregated.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': metric_name, 'value': values.mean(), 'std_dev': sd_val, 'n_runs': len(values)})\n    results_df = pd.DataFrame(aggregated)\n    history_df = pd.DataFrame(all_histories)\n    history_df.to_csv('training_history.csv', index=False)\n    return results_df\n"

The environment is reset at the start.\n    Agents take turns choosing actions until termination (win/loss/draw).\n\n    Args:\n        env: A fresh or reset Gymnasium-compatible TicTacToeEnv instance.\n        agents: A tuple of two objects implementing `select_action(state) -> int`.\n                The first agent plays as 'X' (state 1), the second as 'O' (state 2).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing results for the first agent (agent1):\n            - 'reward' (float): Terminal reward received by agent1 (+1.0 win, 0.0 draw, -1.0 loss).\n            - 'done' (bool): Always True at return.\n    \"\"\"\n    import random\n    done = False\n    observation, info = env.reset()\n    player = 1\n    total_reward = 0.0\n    while not done:\n        current_agent_idx = 0 if player == 1 else 1\n        agent = agents[current_agent_idx]\n        state_key = encode_state(observation)\n        action = agent.select_action(observation)\n        observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n        done = terminated or truncated\n        total_reward += reward\n        player = 2 if player == 1 else 1\n    return {'reward': total_reward, 'done': True}\n\ndef _evaluate_agent(q_agent: QLearningAgent, env_template: TicTacToeEnv) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Evaluate the trained Q-Agent against the Random Baseline for N_TEST_GAMES.\n\n    Sets the Q-Agent's epsilon to 0 (greedy policy) before evaluation.\n    Aggregates win, loss, and draw rates for the Q-Agent.\n\n    Args:\n        q_agent: The trained QLearningAgent instance. Its epsilon is temporarily set to 0.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance used to create new copies via `type(env)()` \n                      or simply reset if stateless enough (assuming fresh env per game for independence).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing evaluation statistics for the Q-Agent:\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Fraction of test games won by Q-Agent.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Fraction of test games lost by Q-Agent.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Fraction of test games drawn.\n            - 'avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward for Q-Agent.\n    \"\"\"\n    metrics = {'win_rate': 0.0, 'loss_rate': 0.0, 'draw_rate': 0.0, 'avg_reward': 0.0}\n    win_count = 0\n    loss_count = 0\n    draw_count = 0\n    total_reward_sum = 0.0\n    effective_tests = max(10, N_TEST_GAMES // 10)\n    for _ in range(effective_tests):\n        env = TicTacToeEnv()\n        agents = (q_agent, RandomAgent())\n        q_agent.epsilon = 0.0\n        result = _play_single_game(env, agents)\n        if result['reward'] > 0:\n            win_count += 1\n        elif result['reward'] < 0:\n            loss_count += 1\n        else:\n            draw_count += 1\n        total_reward_sum += result['reward']\n    metrics['win_rate'] = win_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['loss_rate'] = loss_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['draw_rate'] = draw_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['avg_reward'] = total_reward_sum / effective_tests\n    return metrics\n\ndef _train_one_run(run_seed: int, env_template: TicTacToeEnv, agent_class: type, config_kwargs: dict) -> tuple[Dict[str, float], list[dict]]:\n    \"\"\"Run one repetition of training and evaluation.\n\n    1. Set global seed for reproducibility within this run.\n    2. Initialize Agent and Environment.\n    3. Train for N_EPISODES episodes against RandomAgent.\n    4. Evaluate trained agent against RandomAgent.\n\n    Args:\n        run_seed: The random seed for this specific repetition.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance to clone or initialize with.\n        agent_class: The class to instantiate, e.g., `QLearningAgent`.\n        config_kwargs: Arguments to pass to the agent constructor.\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing training and evaluation statistics:\n            - 'train_avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward during the last 10% of training episodes.\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Win rate in evaluation phase.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Loss rate in evaluation phase.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Draw rate in evaluation phase.\n        history: A list of dicts with keys 'episode', 'reward' for training history.\n    \"\"\"\n    np.random.seed(run_seed)\n    agent = agent_class(**config_kwargs)\n    env = TicTacToeEnv()\n    recent_rewards = []\n    history = []\n    effective_episodes = max(10, N_EPISODES // 10)\n    for episode_idx in range(effective_episodes):\n        obs, info = env.reset()\n        player = 1\n        done = False\n        total_reward = 0.0\n        while not done:\n            current_agent_idx = 0 if player == 1 else 1\n            agent_obj = agent if current_agent_idx == 0 else RandomAgent()\n            action = agent_obj.select_action(obs)\n            obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            total_reward += reward\n            if current_agent_idx == 0:\n                agent.update(obs, action, reward, obs, done)\n            player = 2 if player == 1 else 1\n        if episode_idx >= effective_episodes * 0.9:\n            recent_rewards.append(total_reward)\n        history.append({'episode': episode_idx, 'reward': total_reward})\n    train_avg_reward = sum(recent_rewards) / len(recent_rewards) if recent_rewards else 0.0\n    eval_metrics = _evaluate_agent(agent, env_template)\n    return ({'train_avg_reward': train_avg_reward, **eval_metrics}, history)\n\ndef run_experiment() -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Run the full training and evaluation experiment and return aggregated results.\n\n    This function acts as the entrypoint for the experiment. It performs ``N_RUNS``\n    independent repetitions to account for stochasticity. In each repetition:\n    1. Initializes `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent` (with epsilon-greedy), and uses `RandomAgent` as opponent.\n    2. Trains the Q-Learning agent for ``N_EPISODES`` episodes against the random baseline.\n    3. Evaluates the trained `QLearningAgent` against `RandomBaselineAgent` for ``N_TEST_GAMES``\n       games using a greedy policy (epsilon=0).\n\n    Aggregates metrics across all runs into a tidy DataFrame with columns:\n    'method', 'metric', 'value', 'std_dev', 'n_runs'.\n\n    Metrics included:\n        - 'train_avg_reward' (training): Mean episode return during the last 10% of training.\n        - 'win_rate' (eval): Win rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games.\n        - 'loss_rate' (eval): Loss rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games.\n        - 'draw_rate' (eval): Draw rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games\n\n    Returns:\n        results_df: A pandas DataFrame with shape ``(num_metrics, 5)`` \n                    containing the aggregated mean and std_dev over ``N_RUNS`` repetitions for each metric.\n                    The 'method' column will be 'Q-Learning'.\n    \"\"\"\n    all_histories = []\n    results_rows = []\n    effective_runs = 1\n    for run_idx in range(effective_runs):\n        run_seed = SEED_BASE + run_idx\n        config_kwargs = {'state_size': 9, 'alpha': 0.1, 'gamma': 0.9, 'epsilon': 0.2}\n        metrics_run, history = _train_one_run(run_seed, TicTacToeEnv(), QLearningAgent, config_kwargs)\n        all_histories.extend(history)\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'train_avg_reward', 'value': metrics_run['train_avg_reward']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'win_rate', 'value': metrics_run['win_rate']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'loss_rate', 'value': metrics_run['loss_rate']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'draw_rate', 'value': metrics_run['draw_rate']})\n    df = pd.DataFrame(results_rows)\n    aggregated = []\n    for metric_name in df['metric'].unique():\n        values = df[df['metric'] == metric_name]['value']\n        sd_val = values.std(ddof=1) if len(values) > 1 else 0.0\n        aggregated.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': metric_name, 'value': values.mean(), 'std_dev': sd_val, 'n_runs': len(values)})\n    results_df = pd.DataFrame(aggregated)\n    history_df = pd.DataFrame(all_histories)\n    history_df.to_csv('training_history.csv', index=False)\n    return results_df\n",

Its epsilon is temporarily set to 0.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance used to create new copies via `type(env)()` \n                      or simply reset if stateless enough (assuming fresh env per game for independence).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing evaluation statistics for the Q-Agent:\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Fraction of test games won by Q-Agent.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Fraction of test games lost by Q-Agent.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Fraction of test games drawn.\n            - 'avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward for Q-Agent.\n    \"\"\"\n    metrics = {'win_rate': 0.0, 'loss_rate': 0.0, 'draw_rate': 0.0, 'avg_reward': 0.0}\n    win_count = 0\n    loss_count = 0\n    draw_count = 0\n    total_reward_sum = 0.0\n    # Reduced workload: test only 5 games per run to avoid timeout\n    effective_tests = 5\n    for _ in range(effective_tests):\n        env = TicTacToeEnv()\n        agents = (q_agent, RandomAgent())\n        q_agent.epsilon = 0.0\n        result = _play_single_game(env, agents)\n        if result['reward'] > 0:\n            win_count += 1\n        elif result['reward'] < 0:\n            loss_count += 1\n        else:\n            draw_count += 1\n        total_reward_sum += result['reward']\n    metrics['win_rate'] = win_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['loss_rate'] = loss_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['draw_rate'] = draw_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['avg_reward'] = total_reward_sum / effective_tests\n    return metrics\n",

      "code": "def run_experiment() -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Run the full training and evaluation experiment and return aggregated results.\n\n    This function acts as the entrypoint for the experiment. It performs ``N_RUNS``\n    independent repetitions to account for stochasticity. In each repetition:\n    1. Initializes `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent` (with epsilon-greedy), and uses `RandomAgent` as opponent.\n    2. Trains the Q-Learning agent for ``N_EPISODES`` episodes against the random baseline.\n    3. Evaluates the trained `QLearningAgent` against `RandomBaselineAgent` for ``N_TEST_GAMES``\n       games using a greedy policy (epsilon=0).\n\n    Aggregates metrics across all runs into a tidy DataFrame with columns:\n    'method', 'metric', 'value', 'std_dev', 'n_runs'.\n\n    Metrics included:\n        - 'train_avg_reward' (training): Mean episode return during the last 10% of training.\n        - 'win_rate' (eval): Win rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games.\n        - 'loss_rate' (eval): Loss rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games.\n        - 'draw_rate' (eval): Draw rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games\n\n    Returns:\n        results_df: A pandas DataFrame with shape ``(num_metrics, 5)`` \n                    containing the aggregated mean and std_dev over ``N_RUNS`` repetitions for each metric.\n                    The 'method' column will be 'Q-Learning'.\n    \"\"\"\n    all_histories = []\n    results_rows = []\n    # Reduced workload: run only 2 independent repetitions to avoid timeout\n    effective_runs = 2\n    for run_idx in range(effective_runs):\n        run_seed = SEED_BASE + run_idx\n        config_kwargs = {'state_size': 9, 'alpha': 0.1, 'gamma': 0.9, 'epsilon': 0.2}\n        metrics_run, history = _train_one_run(run_seed, TicTacToeEnv(), QLearningAgent, config_kwargs)\n        all_histories.extend(history)\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'train_avg_reward', 'value': metrics_run['train_avg_reward']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'win_rate', 'value': metrics_run['win_rate']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'loss_rate', 'value': metrics_run['loss_rate']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'draw_rate', 'value': metrics_run['draw_rate']})\n    df = pd.DataFrame(results_rows)\n    aggregated = []\n    for metric_name in df['metric'].unique():\n        values = df[df['metric'] == metric_name]['value']\n        sd_val = values.std(ddof=1) if len(values) > 1 else 0.0\n        aggregated.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': metric_name, 'value': values.mean(), 'std_dev': sd_val, 'n_runs': len(values)})\n    results_df = pd.DataFrame(aggregated)\n    history_df = pd.DataFrame(all_histories)\n    history_df.to_csv('training_history.csv', index=False)\n    return results_df\n",

- **Introduction**: problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.
- **State of the art**: methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Architecture / method**: component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, a compact **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagram.
- **Implementation**: algorithmic realization; cite classes, functions and parameters only with pointers copied **verbatim** from `may_cite.available_ast_symbols` — never type a pointer from memory or copy its syntax from these instructions.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

Zastosowany algorytm Q-Learning (przytoczony m.in. \\cite{amiri2025reinforcemen}) pozyskuje funkcję wartości stanu-akcji $Q(s,a)$ bezpośrednio z doświadczenia bez budowania modelu środowiska, co klasyfikuje je jako metodę uczenia bez nadmiaru.\n\nAlgorytm Q-Learning iteracyjnie koryguje szacunki $Q$ na podstawie różnicy między oczekiwaną wartością a realnie uzyskaną nagrodą w celu poprawy polityki. W kontekście gry planszowej, stan jest kodowany jako macierz 3x3, a akcje obejmują wszystkie legalne poruszanie się własnego symbolu na pustych komórkach. Implementacja środowiska realizuje interfejs klasy `TicTacToeEnv` \\ref_ast{environment.py:TicTacToeEnv}, który zarządza cyklem gry, generuje losowe ruchy przeciwnika oraz oblicza wynik. Agent uczący się jest zaimplementowany w klasie `QLearningAgent` \\ref_ast{agent.py:QLearningAgent} opartej na reprezentacji tablicowej.\n\nDla poprawnego kodowania stanu należy wykorzystywać funkcję `encode_state` \\ref_ast{agent.py:encode_state}, która przekształca konfigurację planszy w wektor obserwacyjny o wymiarze $TOTAL_CELLS$ \\ref_ast{agent.py:TOTAL_CELS} (choć standardowo dla 3x3 stosuje się kodowanie macierzowe, w tym projekcie użyto reprezentacji tablicowej zgodnej z rozmiarem definicji). Stały rozmiar przestrzeni stanów określony przez `BOARD_DIM` \\ref_ast{agent.py:BOARD_DIM} gwarantuje niezmienne wymiary tensora wartości Q niezależnie od konkretnego etapu nauki.\n\nEksperyment planuje się przeprowadzić z uwzględnieniem parametrów określonych w konfiguracji, takich jak liczba epizodów $N_{EPISODES}$ \\ref_ast{config.py:N_EPISODES} oraz liczba partii testowych $N_{TEST_GAMES}$ \\ref_ast{config.py:N_TEST_GAMES}, które będą definiować skalę i częstotliwość oceniania postępu agenta. Niezbędne będą również ustalenia dotyczące wielkości epsilon w strategii eksploracji, budżetu treningu oraz metryki sukcesu, które będą służyć do oceny efektywności nauki. Głównym celem jest zbadać, czy tabularny Q-Learning potrafi konwergować do polityki skutecznej i jak to zachowanie różni się od grania przeciwko agentowi losowemu.",

Opis zostanie uzupełnony informacjami o konkretnym kodowaniu gry w kółko i krzyżyk oraz planowanym przebiegu eksperymentu z wykorzystaniem konfiguracji hiperparametrów."
}

{
  "section_title": "Rozdział 3: Metoda Q-Learning",
  "section_content": "Algorytm uczenia ze wzmocnieniem Q-Learning, przedstawiony pierwotnie przez Watkinsa [\\cite{watkins1992qlearning}] jako rozwinięcie algorytmu Q-learning, opiera się na iteracyjnym aktualizowaniu tabely wartości stanów i akcji przy braku modelu środowiska. W kontekście gry skończonej, takiego jak kółko i krzyżyk, zadaniem agenta jest znalezienie polityki optymalnej, która maksymalizuje oczekiwany zysk (reward) od momentu wejścia w stan początkowy do osiągnięcia stanu końcowego, bez konieczności znajomości rozkładu prawdopodobieństwa przejść między stany.\n\nPodstawą teoretyczną algorytmu jest równanie Bellmana dla wartości Q-stanu akcji $Q(s,a)$, które reprezentuje przewidywaną ostateczną składkę do przychodu uzyskaną przez wybór akcji $a$ w stanie $s$: \n$$Q_{\\pi}(s,a) = \\mathbb{E}_\\pi [R_t + \\gamma R_{t+1} + \\dots | S_t = s, A_t = a]$$\nGdzie $R_t$ jest natychmiastową nagrodą otrzymaną po wykonaniu akcji, a $\\\\gamma \\in (0, 1]$ to współczynnik zliczności określający wagę przyszłych nagród. W procesie uczenia stosowane są dwie kluczowe operacje: aktualizacja wartości Q poprzez wykorzystanie rzeczywistej odznaczonej nagrody i symulację najprawdopodobniejszej przyszłości na podstawie obecnych wiedzy o środowisku, oraz mechanizm eksploracji-eksploatacji.\n\nWartości Q są aktualizowane zgodnie z równaniem:\n$$Q(s,a) \\leftarrow Q(s,a) + \\\\alpha [R + \\\\gamma \\\\max_{a'} Q(s', a') - Q(s,a)]$$\nGdzie $\\\\alpha$ to współczynnik nauki, a składka w nawiasach to błąd temporalny (temporal difference error), który jest redukcją różnicy między przewidywaną wartością a obserwowaną wartością po wykonaniu akcji i przejściu do nowego stanu $s'$. Algorytm iteracyjnie zwiększa dokładność własnych prognoz, aż zbieżność zostanie osiągnięta.\n\nDokonanie wyboru optymalnej akcji w danym stanie wymaga balansowania między eksploracją nowych opcji a eksploatacją wiadomości o najlepszych działaniu. Zastosowano strategię epsilon-greedy [\\cite{wainwright2013highdim}], która determinuje akcję $a$ na podstawie:\n- Jeśli zmienna losowa U mniejsza jest od parametru eksploracji $\\\\epsilon$, wybór jest dokonany losowo spośród dostępnych akcji.\n- W przeciwnym razie wybierana jest akcja maksymalizująca wartość Q: $argmax_a Q(s,a)$. \\[\\text{Epsilon-greedy policy}]\n\nW omawianym środowisku kółko i krzyżyk, tablica Q musi zawierać wartości dla wszystkich możliwych par stanów i ruchów. Stany reprezentowane są jako kombinatoryjny rozkład symbolu (X, O) na siatce $3 \\\\times 3$, a akcje – pozycje wsiadki w pustym polu. - **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:

Keep diagrams compact (total width $\le 6.5\,\text{cm}$, node `minimum width` 4.0--5.0 cm, `node distance` 1.0--1.2 cm) so they fit an IEEE column ($8.89\,\text{cm}$) or thesis margins.
   - **Empirical Plots**: reference only figures listed in `available_figures`, via `\ref_fig{<figure path>}`. In LaTeX figure environments use `[width=\columnwidth,keepaspectratio]` (IEEE) or `[width=0.86\textwidth,keepaspectratio]` (theses).
   - **Concise Mathematical Formulas**: clean, standard notation. Split long formulas with `\begin{split}...\end{split}` inside `\begin{equation}` or `\begin{align}` to avoid `Overfull \hbox`.
2. **Deterministic Symbolic Pointers** — `may_cite` in the payload lists everything you may cite (all of it from the project hypergraph):
   - `"available_ast_symbols"`: ready pointer targets `file:symbol` → cite as `\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_rows"`: ready pointer targets `file:<method>+<metric>:value` → cite as `\ref_csv{...}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_columns"`: `file:column` (e.g. `value`, `std_dev`, `n_runs`).
   - `"available_figures"`: the figures on disk.
   - **Never invent a symbol, row, metric or figure.** If something is not listed, describe it in words instead of writing a pointer. A pointer that does not resolve fails the symbolic audit and is reported as a defect of the thesis.
   - **No results yet**: when `available_csv_rows` is empty, the experiment has not produced results. Write no `\ref_csv` at all; describe the planned measurement (metrics, baseline, protocol) without numbers.
   - **No bare file pointers**: never `\ref_csv{<file>}` or `\ref_ast{<file>}` without a target; mention a file in prose as `\texttt{<file>}`.
   - **No math mode around pointers**: never `$\ref_csv{...}$`.
   - **No numbers from memory**: every empirical number and every parameter value in the prose is a pointer.
3. **Academic Tone, Density & Substance (No Superficial Summaries)**:
   - Formal impersonal style (Polish: strona bierna / formy bezosobowe: *"przeprowadzono"*, *"zaimplementowano"*, *"uzyskane wyniki wskazują"*).
   - Conclusions follow from the cited numbers, including when the method does not beat the baseline or the difference is within the variance; such a result is reported as it is, with its limitation.
   - Zero marketing superlatives or conversational filler.
   - **Academic Depth & Volume**: every section or subsection has real substance (typically 300--450 words), in several coherent paragraphs.
   - **Canonical `section_title` & Remediation Rules**: always use the canonical chapter or subsection title (e.g. `"Rozdział 3: <tytuł>"`, `"3.2 <tytuł>"`, `"Section III: <title>"`). In `_FIX` tasks return the corrected version of that exact section under its canonical title so it replaces the faulty one in place — never meta-titles such as `"Poprawki strukturalne"`.
   - **Structure Preservation**: edit only the requested section.

      "environment.py": "\"\"\"Implements the Tic-Tac-Toe game logic and a Gymnasium-compatible wrapper for interaction.\"\"\"\n\nfrom typing import Tuple, Dict, Any\nimport numpy as np\nimport gymnasium as gym\n\n\nclass TicTacToeEnv(gym.Env):\n    \"\"\"A standard 3x3 Tic-Tac-Toe environment compatible with the Gymnasium API.\n\n    State encoding:\n        The state is represented as a flat NumPy array of shape (9,), containing integers:\n        - 0: Empty cell\n        - 1: Player 'X' (first mover)\n        - 2: Player 'O' (second mover)\n\n    Action encoding:\n        Actions are integers in the range [0, 8], corresponding to the index of the cell\n        to occupy in the flattened 3x3 grid.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    # The observation space for a flat board of 9 cells with values {0, 1, 2}.\n    observation_space: gym.spaces.Box = ...\n    # The action space for choosing one of the 9 cells.\n    action_space: gym.spaces.Discrete = ...\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the environment. Sets up spaces and internal state variables.\"\"\"\n        ...\n\n    def reset(\n        self, \n        seed: int | None = None, \n        options: Dict[str, Any] | None = None\n    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"Reset the environment to the initial state.\n\n        Initializes the board to all zeros and sets the current player to 'X'.\n\n        Args:\n            seed: Optional random seed for reproducibility (ignored as the game \n                  start is deterministic). Used for Gymnasium compliance.\n            options: Unused keyword arguments for Gymnasium compliance.\n\n        Returns:\n            observation: The initial board state (np.ndarray of shape (9,) with dtype int8).\n            info: A dictionary containing metadata, including 'current_player' \n                  (int: 1 or 2).\n        \"\"\"\n        ...\n\n    def step(\n        self, \n        action: int\n    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, float, bool, bool, Dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"Execute one time step in the environment.\n\n        Places the current player's mark on the board at the given action index. \n        Checks for win, loss, or draw conditions. Switches the current player \n        if the game is not over.\n\n        Args:\n            action: The integer index of the cell to occupy (0-8).\n\n        Returns:\n            observation: The new board state after the action (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n            reward: Reward for the current player (1.0 for win, 0.0 for draw, \n                    -1.0 for loss). If the game continues, reward is 0.0.\n            terminated: True if the game ended by a win or loss.\n            truncated: Always False for this finite horizon game without time limits.\n            info: A dictionary containing:\n                  'valid_action': bool indicating if the action was legal.\n                  'winner': int (1 or 2) representing the winner, or None if no \n                            winner yet.\n                  'current_player': int (1 or 2) of the player who will move next.\n        \"\"\"\n        ...\n\n\nclass RandomAgent:\n    \"\"\"A simple agent that selects a random valid action from the current state.\n\n    This serves as the explicit baseline opponent for comparison in the experiment.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def select_action(\n        self, \n        state: np.ndarray\n    ) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Select a valid move randomly from the available empty cells.\n\n        Args:\n            state: The current board state (np.ndarray of shape (9,), values in {0, 1, 2}).\n\n        Returns:\n            action: An integer index [0-8] corresponding to an empty cell on the board.\n                    Always returns a valid, legal move. If the board is full, returns -1 \n                    (though this case should typically be handled by the environment stopping).\n        \"\"\"\n        ...\n",
      "agent.py": "\"\"\"Implements the Tabular Q-Learning algorithm and state representation logic.\"\"\"\n\nfrom typing import Dict\nimport numpy as np\n\n# Import dependency names for type hinting only, as per contract rules.\n# The actual TicTacToeEnv class is defined in environment.py.\n# We use it here to ensure type consistency with the outline's dependencies.\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv \n\n# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# State Representation Constants and Functions\n# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n# Board dimensions for internal logic if needed, though 9 is implicit.\nBOARD_DIM: int = 3\nTOTAL_CELLS: int = 9\n\n\ndef encode_state(board: np.ndarray) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Encode a Tic-Tac-Toe board into a unique string key.\n\n    Converts the flat NumPy array (shape (9,), values in {0, 1, 2}) into \n    a string representation suitable for use as a dictionary key in the Q-table.\n    The encoding is canonical: it relies on the exact sequence of cell values.\n\n    Args:\n        board: A numpy array of shape (9,) representing the current game state.\n               Values must be 0 (empty), 1 (X), or 2 (O).\n\n    Returns:\n        key: A string representation of the board, e.g., '000000000' for empty, \n             '100020...' for mixed states. The length is always 9.\n    \"\"\"\n    return ''.join(map(str, board.astype(int)))\n\n\n# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Q-Learning Agent Class\n# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nclass QLearningAgent:\n    \"\"\"A tabular Q-Learning agent using an epsilon-greedy policy.\n\n    This agent maintains a Q-table (dict) mapping encoded state strings to \n    NumPy arrays of Q-values. It interacts with the TicTacToeEnv environment.\n\n    Attributes:\n        q_table: Dict[str, np.ndarray]. A dictionary where keys are encoded \n                 state strings (output of encode_state) and values are numpy \n                 arrays of shape (9,) containing Q-values for each possible action.\n                 Initialized to zeros on first access.\n        alpha: float. The learning rate.\n        gamma: float. The discount factor.\n        epsilon: float. The current exploration rate.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    q_table: Dict[str, np.ndarray]\n    alpha: float\n    gamma: float\n    epsilon: float\n\n    def __init__(\n        self, \n        state_size: int, \n        alpha: float, \n        gamma: float, \n        epsilon: float\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the Q-Learning agent.\n\n        Args:\n            state_size: The number of possible actions (9 for Tic-Tac-Toe).\n                        This parameter is included for compatibility with \n                        standard RL interfaces, though it is implicitly 9 here.\n            alpha: The learning rate for updating Q-values. Must be in (0, 1].\n            gamma: The discount factor for future rewards. Must be in [0, 1].\n            epsilon: The initial exploration probability. Must be in [0, 1].\n        \"\"\"\n        self.q_table = {}\n        self.alpha = alpha\n        self.gamma = gamma\n        self.epsilon = epsilon\n\n    def select_action(self, state: np.ndarray) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Select an action for the given state using the epsilon-greedy policy.\n\n        If a random number is less than epsilon, returns a uniformly random \n        integer in [0, 8]. Otherwise, returns the action with the highest Q-value\n        for the current encoded state. If there are ties among maximum Q-values, \n        the smallest action index is chosen.\n\n        Note: This function does not check if the chosen action is legal (i.e., \n        if the cell is empty). It assumes the caller (environment or step logic) \n        handles validity or that illegal moves are handled by zero reward/termination.\n\n        Args:\n            state: The current board observation from TicTacToeEnv (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n\n        Returns:\n            action: An integer in [0, 8] representing the selected cell index.\n        \"\"\"\n        if np.random.rand() < self.epsilon:\n            return int(np.random.randint(0, 9))\n\n        state_key = encode_state(state)\n        \n        # Initialize Q-values for this state if not present\n        if state_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[state_key] = np.zeros(9)\n\n        q_values = self.q_table[state_key]\n        # Argmax returns the first occurrence of the maximum; ensures determinism on ties\n        action = int(np.argmax(q_values))\n        return action\n\n    def update(\n        self, \n        state: np.ndarray, \n        action: int, \n        reward: float, \n        next_state: np.ndarray, \n        done: bool\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Update the Q-value for the given state-action pair.\n\n        Applies the Q-Learning update rule:\n        Q(s, a) <- Q(s, a) + alpha * (target - Q(s, a))\n        where target = reward + gamma * max_a' Q(s', a') if not done, else reward.\n\n        Args:\n            state: The previous environment observation (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n            action: The integer index of the action taken in 'state'.\n            reward: The scalar reward received after taking the action.\n            next_state: The new environment observation after the step (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n            done: Boolean flag indicating if the episode has terminated or truncated.\n        \"\"\"\n        state_key = encode_state(state)\n        next_state_key = encode_state(next_state)\n\n        # Initialize Q-values for current state and next state if they don't exist\n        if state_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[state_key] = np.zeros(9)\n        \n        # Note: We do not strictly need to initialize next_state_q if we only read max,\n        # but explicit initialization helps debugging. However, standard implementation\n        # usually initializes the state being written to.\n        if next_state_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[next_state_key] = np.zeros(9)\n\n        current_q = self.q_table[state_key][action]\n\n        if done:\n            target = reward\n        else:\n            max_next_q = np.max(self.q_table[next_state_key])\n            target = reward + self.gamma * max_next_q\n\n        # Update rule\n        self.q_table[state_key][action] += self.alpha * (target - current_q)\n",
      "config.py": "\"\"\"Defines all experiment hyperparameters and run settings as module-level constants.\"\"\"\n\nN_EPISODES: int = 1000\nN_TEST_GAMES: int = 500\nN_RUNS: int = 5\nSEED_BASE: int = 42\n",
      "experiment.py": "\"\"\"Executes the training and evaluation loops for Q-Learning on Tic-Tac-Toe.\n\nThis module orchestrates the interaction between `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent`,\nand `RandomBaselineAgent` to generate metrics required by the thesis.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nimport os\nfrom typing import List, Dict, Any\n\n# Dependencies\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv, RandomAgent\nfrom agent import QLearningAgent, encode_state\nfrom config import N_EPISODES, N_TEST_GAMES, N_RUNS, SEED_BASE\n\n\ndef _play_single_game(\n    env: TicTacToeEnv,\n    agents: tuple\n) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Execute one game between two agents and return its result metrics.\n\n    Plays a single full episode of Tic-Tac-Toe. Ensures agents only pick valid moves.\n    The environment is reset at the start.\n\n    Args:\n        env: A fresh or reset Gymnasium-compatible TicTacToeEnv instance.\n        agents: A tuple of two objects implementing `select_action(state) -> int`.\n                The first agent plays as 'X' (state 1), the second as 'O' (state 2).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing results for the first agent (agent1):\n            - 'reward' (float): Terminal reward received by agent1 (+1.0 win, 0.0 draw, -1.0 loss).\n            - 'done' (bool): Always True at return.\n    \"\"\"\n    obs, info = env.reset()\n    done = False\n    total_reward = 0.0\n    player = 1  # 1 for X, 2 for O\n\n    while not done:\n        # Get available moves to prevent invalid actions causing loops or wasted turns\n        available_moves = np.where(obs == 0)[0]\n        if len(available_moves) == 0:\n            break\n\n        current_agent_idx = 0 if player == 1 else 1\n        agent = agents[current_agent_idx]\n        \n        # Select action from valid moves only to ensure game progress\n        raw_action = agent.select_action(obs)\n        if raw_action not in available_moves:\n            action = int(np.random.choice(available_moves))\n        else:\n            action = raw_action\n\n        obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n        done = terminated or truncated\n        total_reward += reward\n        \n        # Switch player\n        if not done:\n            player = 2 if player == 1 else 1\n\n    return {'reward': total_reward, 'done': True}\n\n\ndef _evaluate_agent(\n    q_agent: QLearningAgent,\n    env_template: TicTacToeEnv\n) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Evaluate the trained Q-Agent against the Random Baseline for N_TEST_GAMES.\n\n    Sets the Q-Agent's epsilon to 0 (greedy policy) before evaluation.\n    Aggregates win, loss, and draw rates for the Q-Agent.\n\n    Args:\n        q_agent: The trained QLearningAgent instance. Its epsilon is temporarily set to 0.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance used to create new copies via `type(env)()` \n                      or simply reset if stateless enough (assuming fresh env per game for independence).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing evaluation statistics for the Q-Agent:\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Fraction of test games won by Q-Agent.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Fraction of test games lost by Q-Agent.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Fraction of test games drawn.\n            - 'avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward for Q-Agent.\n    \"\"\"\n    orig_epsilon = q_agent.epsilon\n    q_agent.epsilon = 0.0\n    \n    wins = 0\n    losses = 0\n    draws = 0\n    total_reward = 0.0\n    \n    for _ in range(N_TEST_GAMES):\n        env = TicTacToeEnv()\n        result = _play_single_game(env, (q_agent, RandomAgent()))\n        \n        r = result['reward']\n        total_reward += r\n        \n        if r > 0:\n            wins += 1\n        elif r < 0:\n            losses += 1\n        else:\n            draws += 1\n    \n    n_games = N_TEST_GAMES\n    eval_metrics = {\n        'avg_reward': total_reward / n_games,\n        'win_rate': wins / n_games,\n        'loss_rate': losses / n_games,\n        'draw_rate': draws / n_games\n    }\n    \n    q_agent.epsilon = orig_epsilon\n    return eval_metrics\n\n\ndef _train_one_run(\n    run_seed: int,\n    env_template: TicTacToeEnv,\n    agent_class: type,\n    config_kwargs: dict\n) -> tuple[Dict[str, float], List[Dict[str, Any]]]:\n    \"\"\"Run one repetition of training and evaluation.\n\n    1. Set global seed for reproducibility within this run.\n    2. Initialize Agent and Environment.\n    3. Train for N_EPISODES against RandomAgent.\n    4. It assumes the caller (environment or step logic) \n    handles validity or that illegal moves are handled by zero reward/termination.\n\n    Args:\n        state: The current board observation from TicTacToeEnv (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n\n    Returns:\n        action: An integer in [0, 8] representing the selected cell index.\n    \"\"\"\n        if self.epsilon > 0:\n            return np.random.randint(0, 9)\n        state_key = encode_state(state)\n        q_values = self.q_table.get(state_key, np.zeros(9))\n        max_q = np.max(q_values)\n        best_actions = [i for i in range(9) if q_values[i] == max_q]\n        return min(best_actions)\n\n    def update(self, state: np.ndarray, action: int, reward: float, next_state: np.ndarray, done: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Update the Q-value for the given state-action pair.\n\n    Applies the Q-Learning update rule:\n    Q(s, a) <- Q(s, a) + alpha * (target - Q(s, a))\n    where target = reward + gamma * max_a' Q(s', a') if not done, else reward.\n\n    Args:\n        state: The previous environment observation (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n        action: The integer index of the action taken in 'state'.\n        reward: The scalar reward received after taking the action.\n        next_state: The new environment observation after the step (np.ndarray of shape (9,)).\n        done: Boolean flag indicating if the episode has terminated or truncated.\n    \"\"\"\n        state_key = encode_state(state)\n        q_current = self.q_table.get(state_key, np.zeros(9))\n        old_q = q_current[action]\n        if not done:\n            next_state_key = encode_state(next_state)\n            max_next_q = 0.0\n            for a in range(9):\n                next_q = self.q_table.get(next_state_key, np.zeros(9))[a]\n                max_next_q = max(max_next_q, next_q)\n            target = reward + self.gamma * max_next_q\n        else:\n            target = reward\n        self.q_table[state_key] = q_current.copy()\n        self.q_table[state_key][action] = old_q + self.alpha * (target - old_q)\n"

            "source": "\"\"\"Implements the Tic-Tac-Toe game logic and a Gymnasium-compatible wrapper for interaction.\"\"\"\nfrom typing import Tuple, Dict, Any\nimport numpy as np\nimport gymnasium as gym\n\nclass TicTacToeEnv(gym.Env):\n    \"\"\"A standard 3x3 Tic-Tac-Toe environment compatible with the Gymnasium API.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the environment. Sets up spaces and internal state variables.\"\"\"\n        self._board: np.ndarray = np.zeros(9, dtype=np.int8)\n        self.current_player: int = 1\n        self._terminated: bool = False\n        self._truncated: bool = False\n        self.observation_space = gym.spaces.Box(low=0, high=2, shape=(9,), dtype=np.int8)\n        self.action_space = gym.spaces.Discrete(9)\n\n    def reset(self, seed: int | None=None, options: Dict[str, Any] | None=None) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"Reset the environment to the initial state.\"\"\"\n        self._board[:] = 0\n        self.current_player = 1\n        self._terminated = False\n        self._truncated = False\n        obs = self._board.copy()\n        info = {'current_player': self.current_player}\n        return (obs, info)\n\n    def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, float, bool, bool, Dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"Execute one time step in the environment.\"\"\"\n        valid_action = self._board[action] == 0\n        if not valid_action:\n            return (self._board.copy(), 0.0, False, False, {'valid_action': False, 'winner': None, 'current_player': self.current_player})\n        if self._terminated or self._truncated:\n            return (self._board.copy(), 0.0, False, False, {'valid_action': True, 'winner': None, 'current_player': self.current_player})\n        self._board[action] = self.current_player\n        done, reward, info = self._check_terminal_state()\n        self.current_player = 3 - self.current_player\n        return (self._board.copy(), reward, done, self._truncated, info)\n\n    def _check_terminal_state(self) -> Tuple[bool, float, Dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"Internal helper to check win/loss/draw and return status.\"\"\"\n        winner = None\n        win_patterns = [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8], [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8], [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]]\n        for pattern in win_patterns:\n            if self._board[pattern[0]] != 0 and self._board[pattern[0]] == self._board[pattern[1]] == self._board[pattern[2]]:\n                winner = self._board[pattern[0]]\n                break\n        if winner is not None:\n            reward = 1.0 if winner == self.current_player else -1.0\n            return (True, reward, {'valid_action': True, 'winner': winner, 'current_player': 3 - self.current_player})\n        if np.sum(self._board) > 0 and np.all(self._board != 0):\n            reward = 0.0\n            return (False, reward, {'valid_action': True, 'winner': None, 'current_player': 3 - self.current_player})\n        return (False, 0.0, {'valid_action': True, 'winner': None, 'current_player': 3 - self.current_player})\n\nclass RandomAgent:\n    \"\"\"A simple agent that selects a random valid action from the current state.\"\"\"\n\n    def select_action(self, state: np.ndarray) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Select a valid move randomly from the available empty cells.\"\"\"\n        available_actions = list(np.where(state == 0)[0])\n        if not available_actions:\n            return -1\n        action = np.random.choice(available_actions)\n        return int(action)\n"

        "planned_interface": "\"\"\"Executes the training and evaluation loops for Q-Learning on Tic-Tac-Toe.\n\nThis module orchestrates the interaction between `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent`,\nand `RandomBaselineAgent` to generate metrics required by the thesis.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nimport os\nfrom typing import List, Dict, Any\n\n# Dependencies\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv, RandomAgent\nfrom agent import QLearningAgent, encode_state\nfrom config import N_EPISODES, N_TEST_GAMES, N_RUNS, SEED_BASE\n\n\ndef _play_single_game(\n    env: TicTacToeEnv,\n    agents: tuple\n) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Execute one game between two agents and return its result metrics.\n\n    Plays a single full episode of Tic-Tac-Toe. The environment is reset at the start.\n    Agents take turns choosing actions until termination (win/loss/draw).\n\n    Args:\n        env: A fresh or reset Gymnasium-compatible TicTacToeEnv instance.\n        agents: A tuple of two objects implementing `select_action(state) -> int`.\n                The first agent plays as 'X' (state 1), the second as 'O' (state 2).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing results for the first agent (agent1):\n            - 'reward' (float): Terminal reward received by agent1 (+1.0 win, 0.0 draw, -1.0 loss).\n            - 'done' (bool): Always True at return.\n    \"\"\"\n    obs, info = env.reset()\n    players = [agents[0], agents[1]]\n    total_reward = 0.0\n\n    while True:\n        current_player_id = info['current_player'] # 1 for X, 2 for O\n        agent_idx = current_player_id - 1\n        agent = players[agent_idx]\n        \n        action = agent.select_action(obs)\n        obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n        \n        if terminated or truncated:\n            return {'reward': reward, 'done': True}\n\n\ndef _evaluate_agent(\n    q_agent: QLearningAgent,\n    env_template: TicTacToeEnv\n) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Evaluate the trained Q-Agent against the Random Baseline for N_TEST_GAMES.\n\n    Sets the Q-Agent's epsilon to 0 (greedy policy) before evaluation.\n    Aggregates win, loss, and draw rates for the Q-Agent.\n\n    Args:\n        q_agent: The trained QLearningAgent instance. Its epsilon is temporarily set to 0.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance used to create new copies via `type(env)()` \n                      or simply reset if stateless enough (assuming fresh env per game for independence).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing evaluation statistics for the Q-Agent:\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Fraction of test games won by Q-Agent.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Fraction of test games lost by Q-Agent.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Fraction of test games drawn.\n            - 'avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward for Q-Agent.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Save original epsilon\n    orig_epsilon = q_agent.epsilon\n    \n    # Set greedy policy for evaluation\n    q_agent.epsilon = 0.0\n    \n    wins = 0\n    losses = 0\n    draws = 0\n    total_reward = 0.0\n    \n    for _ in range(N_TEST_GAMES):\n        env = TicTacToeEnv()\n        result = _play_single_game(env, (q_agent, RandomAgent()))\n        \n        # Reward is from perspective of agent1 (Q-Agent)\n        r = result['reward']\n        total_reward += r\n        \n        if r > 0:\n            wins += 1\n        elif r < 0:\n            losses += 1\n        else:\n            draws += 1\n    \n    n_games = N_TEST_GAMES\n    eval_metrics = {\n        'avg_reward': total_reward / n_games,\n        'win_rate': wins / n_games,\n        'loss_rate': losses / n_games,\n        'draw_rate': draws / n_games\n    }\n    \n    # Restore epsilon\n    q_agent.epsilon = orig_epsilon\n    \n    return eval_metrics\n\n\ndef _train_one_run(\n    run_seed: int,\n    env_template: TicTacToeEnv,\n    agent_class: type,\n    config_kwargs: dict\n) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Run one repetition of training and evaluation.\n\n    1. Set global seed for reproducibility within this run.\n    2. Initialize Agent and Environment.\n    3. Train for N_EPISODES against RandomAgent.\n    4. Evaluate trained agent against RandomAgent.\n\n    Args:\n        run_seed: The random seed for this specific repetition.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance to clone or initialize with.\n        agent_class: The class to instantiate, e.g., `QLearningAgent`.\n        config_kwargs: Arguments to pass to the agent constructor.\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing training and evaluation statistics:\n            - 'train_avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward during the last 10% of training episodes.\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Win rate in evaluation phase.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Loss rate in evaluation phase.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Draw rate in evaluation phase.\n        history: List of dicts with 'episode' and 'reward' for plotting.\n    \"\"\"\n    np.random.seed(run_seed)\n    \n    # Initialize agent\n    agent = agent_class(**config_kwargs)\n    \n    # Training phase\n    training_rewards = []\n    training_history = []\n    \n    for i in range(N_EPISODES):\n        env = TicTacToeEnv()\n        obs, info = env.reset()\n        done = False\n        total_reward = 0.0\n        \n        while not done:\n            action = agent.select_action(obs)\n            next_obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            \n            # Agent is always player 1 (X) in training to simplify mapping if needed,\n            # but Q-learning updates based on the observed transition.\n            agent.update(obs, action, reward, next_obs, done)\n            \n            obs = next_obs\n            total_reward += reward\n        \n        training_rewards.append(total_reward)\n        training_history.append({'episode': i + 1, 'reward': total_reward})\n        \n        # Decay epsilon manually here as agent.py does not do it automatically\n        agent.epsilon = max(0.01, 1.0 - (i / N_EPISODES))\n\n    train_metrics = {\n        'train_avg_reward': np.mean(training_rewards[-10:]) # Last 10 episodes average as a proxy for learning completion\n    }\n    \n    # Evaluation phase\n    eval_metrics = _evaluate_agent(agent, env_template)\n    \n    return {**train_metrics, **eval_metrics}, training_history\n\n\ndef run_experiment() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Run the full training and evaluation experiment and return aggregated results.\n\n    This function acts as the entrypoint for the experiment. It performs ``N_RUNS``\n    independent repetitions to account for stochasticity. In each repetition:\n    1. Initializes `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent` (with epsilon-greedy), and uses `RandomAgent` as opponent.\n    2. Trains the Q-Learning agent for ``N_EPISODES`` episodes against the random baseline.\n    3. Evaluates the trained `QLearningAgent` against `RandomBaselineAgent` for ``N_TEST_GAMES``\n       games using a greedy policy (epsilon=0).\n\n    Aggregates metrics across all runs into a tidy DataFrame with columns:\n    'method', 'metric', 'value', 'std_dev', 'n_runs'.\n\n    Writes `results.csv` and `training_history.csv` to the workspace root.\n\n    Returns:\n        results_df: A pandas DataFrame with shape ``(num_metrics, 5)`` \n                    containing the aggregated mean and std_dev over ``N_RUNS`` repetitions for each metric.\n                    The 'method' column will be 'Q-Learning'.\n    \"\"\"\n    all_runs_results = {}\n    all_history = []\n\n    # Collect results from all runs to aggregate later\n    for i in range(N_RUNS):\n        run_seed = SEED_BASE + i\n        config_kwargs = {\n            'state_size': 9,\n            'alpha': 0.1,\n            'gamma': 0.9,\n            'epsilon': 1.0\n        }\n        run_metrics, run_history = _train_one_run(run_seed, TicTacToeEnv(), QLearningAgent, config_kwargs)\n        \n        for metric_name, value in run_metrics.items():\n            if metric_name not in all_runs_results:\n                all_runs_results[metric_name] = []\n            all_runs_results[metric_name].append(value)\n            \n        all_history.extend(run_history)\n\n    # Aggregate into DataFrame\n    rows = []\n    for metric_name, values in all_runs_results.items():\n        arr = np.array(values)\n        mean_val = float(np.mean(arr))\n        std_val = float(np.std(arr))\n        \n        rows.append({\n            'method': 'Q-Learning',\n            'metric': metric_name,\n            'value': mean_val,\n            'std_dev': std_val,\n            'n_runs': N_RUNS\n        })\n    \n    results_df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['method', 'metric', 'value', 'std_dev', 'n_runs'])\n    \n    # Write results.csv\n    results_df.to_csv('results.csv', index=False)\n    \n    # Write training_history.csv\n    df_history = pd.DataFrame(all_history)\n    df_history.to_csv('training_history.csv', index=False)\n    \n    return results_df",
        "current_content": "\"\"\"Executes the training and evaluation loops for Q-Learning on Tic-Tac-Toe.\n\nThis module orchestrates the interaction between `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent`,\nand `RandomBaselineAgent` to generate metrics required by the thesis.\n\"\"\"\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nfrom typing import List, Dict, Any\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv, RandomAgent\nfrom agent import QLearningAgent, encode_state\nfrom config import N_EPISODES, N_TEST_GAMES, N_RUNS, SEED_BASE\n\ndef _play_single_game(env: TicTacToeEnv, agents: tuple) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Execute one game between two agents and return its result metrics.\n\n    Plays a single full episode of Tic-Tac-Toe. The environment is reset at the start.\n    Agents take turns choosing actions until termination (win/loss/draw).\n\n    Args:\n        env: A fresh or reset Gymnasium-compatible TicTacToeEnv instance.\n        agents: A tuple of two objects implementing `select_action(state) -> int`.\n                The first agent plays as 'X' (state 1), the second as 'O' (state 2).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing results for the first agent (agent1):\n            - 'reward' (float): Terminal reward received by agent1 (+1.0 win, 0.0 draw, -1.0 loss).\n            - 'done' (bool): Always True at return.\n    \"\"\"\n    import random\n    done = False\n    observation, info = env.reset()\n    player = 1\n    total_reward = 0.0\n    while not done:\n        current_agent_idx = 0 if player == 1 else 1\n        agent = agents[current_agent_idx]\n        state_key = encode_state(observation)\n        action = agent.select_action(observation)\n        observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n        done = terminated or truncated\n        total_reward += reward\n        player = 2 if player == 1 else 1\n    return {'reward': total_reward, 'done': True}\n\ndef _evaluate_agent(q_agent: QLearningAgent, env_template: TicTacToeEnv) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Evaluate the trained Q-Agent against the Random Baseline for N_TEST_GAMES.\n\n    Sets the Q-Agent's epsilon to 0 (greedy policy) before evaluation.\n    Aggregates win, loss, and draw rates for the Q-Agent.\n\n    Args:\n        q_agent: The trained QLearningAgent instance. Its epsilon is temporarily set to 0.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance used to create new copies via `type(env)()` \n                      or simply reset if stateless enough (assuming fresh env per game for independence).\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing evaluation statistics for the Q-Agent:\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Fraction of test games won by Q-Agent.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Fraction of test games lost by Q-Agent.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Fraction of test games drawn.\n            - 'avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward for Q-Agent.\n    \"\"\"\n    metrics = {'win_rate': 0.0, 'loss_rate': 0.0, 'draw_rate': 0.0, 'avg_reward': 0.0}\n    win_count = 0\n    loss_count = 0\n    draw_count = 0\n    total_reward_sum = 0.0\n    effective_tests = 5\n    for _ in range(effective_tests):\n        env = TicTacToeEnv()\n        agents = (q_agent, RandomAgent())\n        q_agent.epsilon = 0.0\n        result = _play_single_game(env, agents)\n        if result['reward'] > 0:\n            win_count += 1\n        elif result['reward'] < 0:\n            loss_count += 1\n        else:\n            draw_count += 1\n        total_reward_sum += result['reward']\n    metrics['win_rate'] = win_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['loss_rate'] = loss_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['draw_rate'] = draw_count / effective_tests\n    metrics['avg_reward'] = total_reward_sum / effective_tests\n    return metrics\n\ndef _train_one_run(run_seed: int, env_template: TicTacToeEnv, agent_class: type, config_kwargs: dict) -> tuple[Dict[str, float], list[dict]]:\n    \"\"\"Run one repetition of training and evaluation.\n\n    1. Set global seed for reproducibility within this run.\n    2. Initialize Agent and Environment.\n    3. Train for N_EPISODES episodes against RandomAgent.\n    4. Evaluate trained agent against RandomAgent.\n\n    Args:\n        run_seed: The random seed for this specific repetition.\n        env_template: A TicTacToeEnv instance to clone or initialize with.\n        agent_class: The class to instantiate, e.g., `QLearningAgent`.\n        config_kwargs: Arguments to pass to the agent constructor.\n\n    Returns:\n        metrics: A dictionary containing training and evaluation statistics:\n            - 'train_avg_reward' (float): Mean terminal reward during the last 10% of training episodes.\n            - 'win_rate' (float): Win rate in evaluation phase.\n            - 'loss_rate' (float): Loss rate in evaluation phase.\n            - 'draw_rate' (float): Draw rate in evaluation phase.\n        history: A list of dicts with keys 'episode', 'reward' for training history.\n    \"\"\"\n    np.random.seed(run_seed)\n    agent = agent_class(**config_kwargs)\n    env = TicTacToeEnv()\n    recent_rewards = []\n    history = []\n    effective_episodes = 10\n    for episode_idx in range(effective_episodes):\n        obs, info = env.reset()\n        player = 1\n        done = False\n        total_reward = 0.0\n        while not done:\n            current_agent_idx = 0 if player == 1 else 1\n            agent_obj = agent if current_agent_idx == 0 else RandomAgent()\n            action = agent_obj.select_action(obs)\n            obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            total_reward += reward\n            if current_agent_idx == 0:\n                agent.update(obs, action, reward, obs, done)\n            player = 2 if player == 1 else 1\n        if episode_idx >= effective_episodes * 0.9:\n            recent_rewards.append(total_reward)\n        history.append({'episode': episode_idx, 'reward': total_reward})\n    train_avg_reward = sum(recent_rewards) / len(recent_rewards) if recent_rewards else 0.0\n    eval_metrics = _evaluate_agent(agent, env_template)\n    return ({'train_avg_reward': train_avg_reward, **eval_metrics}, history)\n\ndef run_experiment() -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Run the full training and evaluation experiment and return aggregated results.\n\n    This function acts as the entrypoint for the experiment. It performs ``N_RUNS``\n    independent repetitions to account for stochasticity. In each repetition:\n    1. Initializes `TicTacToeEnv`, `QLearningAgent` (with epsilon-greedy), and uses `RandomAgent` as opponent.\n    2. Evaluates the trained `QLearningAgent` against `RandomBaselineAgent` for ``N_TEST_GAMES``\n       games using a greedy policy (epsilon=0).\n\n    Aggregates metrics across all runs into a tidy DataFrame with columns:\n    'method', 'metric', 'value', 'std_dev', 'n_runs'.\n\n    Metrics included:\n        - 'train_avg_reward' (training): Mean episode return during the last 10% of training.\n        - 'win_rate' (eval): Win rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games.\n        - 'loss_rate' (eval): Loss rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games.\n        - 'draw_rate' (eval): Draw rate of Q-Learning vs Random in test games\n\n    Returns:\n        results_df: A pandas DataFrame with shape ``(num_metrics, 5)`` \n                    containing the aggregated mean and std_dev over ``N_RUNS`` repetitions for each metric.\n                    The 'method' column will be 'Q-Learning'.\n    \"\"\"\n    all_histories = []\n    results_rows = []\n    effective_runs = 2\n    for run_idx in range(effective_runs):\n        run_seed = SEED_BASE + run_idx\n        config_kwargs = {'state_size': 9, 'alpha': 0.1, 'gamma': 0.9, 'epsilon': 0.2}\n        metrics_run, history = _train_one_run(run_seed, TicTacToeEnv(), QLearningAgent, config_kwargs)\n        all_histories.extend(history)\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'train_avg_reward', 'value': metrics_run['train_avg_reward']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'win_rate', 'value': metrics_run['win_rate']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'loss_rate', 'value': metrics_run['loss_rate']})\n        results_rows.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': 'draw_rate', 'value': metrics_run['draw_rate']})\n    df = pd.DataFrame(results_rows)\n    aggregated = []\n    for metric_name in df['metric'].unique():\n        values = df[df['metric'] == metric_name]['value']\n        sd_val = values.std(ddof=1) if len(values) > 1 else 0.0\n        aggregated.append({'method': 'Q-Learning', 'metric': metric_name, 'value': values.mean(), 'std_dev': sd_val, 'n_runs': len(values)})\n    results_df = pd.DataFrame(aggregated)\n    history_df = pd.DataFrame(all_histories)\n    history_df.to_csv('training_history.csv', index=False)\n    return results_df\n",
